one_line: A point prompt's normalized distance-to-boundary acts as SAM's hidden granularity dial: click position, not semantics, decides part-vs-whole.
problem: [KNOWN FACT] SAM returns multiple candidate masks per point prompt to handle part/whole ambiguity, but what actually controls which granularity wins is not characterized.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] SAM's part-vs-whole selection is predicted primarily by the click's normalized distance to the nearest strong boundary, and this geometric rule dominates over object category or context.
falsifiable_prediction: Sweeping a click from object center to boundary will produce part/whole flips at a consistent normalized-distance threshold that transfers across unrelated categories; a purely geometric regressor on click position will predict the selected granularity far above chance.
why_important: If granularity is a geometric artifact, interactive annotation tools and pseudo-labeling pipelines built on SAM inherit a systematic, correctable bias, and 'prompt engineering' for segmentation becomes a measurable science instead of folklore.
why_possibly_novel: [HYPOTHESIS] SAM ambiguity is usually described as a property of the image; framing granularity selection as a learned geometric prior of the prompt encoder appears untested.
minimal_falsification_experiment: Take ~200 images with part/whole ground-truth pairs (e.g., person/torso, car/wheel), densely sample click positions per object, record which SAM multimask output ranks first, and fit a geometric-only predictor vs a semantic-only predictor of the outcome.
main_risk: Granularity choice may be governed by an entangled mix of geometry and appearance, making the clean threshold unmeasurable.
community_default_belief: The community treats SAM's multimask output as resolving an intrinsic image ambiguity, with the top-ranked mask reflecting the most salient object interpretation. [KNOWN FACT] that SAM emits 3 candidates; the salience interpretation is folklore.
why_that_may_be_wrong: The prompt encoder only sees a positional encoding of the click; the decoder may have learned a shortcut mapping click-to-boundary distance onto SA-1B's mask-size statistics rather than any salience computation.
fastest_falsification: One afternoon: 20 objects, 20 click positions each, plot chosen-mask relative area vs normalized click distance; absence of a monotone relationship kills the hypothesis.

consolidation.territory: T01 SAM / Foundation Model adaptation / PEFT

one_line: Box prompts beat point prompts mostly because they leak scale, not localization: a point plus a scale hint recovers most of the gap.
problem: [KNOWN FACT] Box prompts consistently outperform single points for SAM across reported evaluations, but the mechanism (localization vs scale disambiguation) is unattributed.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Most of the box advantage is the scale information it carries; localization contributes a minor share.
falsifiable_prediction: Augmenting a single point prompt with a scale-only signal (e.g., a centered disk mask prompt of the correct area, or a degenerate box of correct size at imprecise position) will recover the majority of the point-to-box IoU gap across datasets.
why_important: Determines what interactive systems should ask humans for (a cheap size estimate vs an exact box) and what automatic prompters must predict; reframes 'better prompts' as 'inject scale'.
why_possibly_novel: [HYPOTHESIS] Decompositions of prompt information content (scale vs position vs extent) for SAM appear unstudied; papers compare prompt types wholesale.
minimal_falsification_experiment: On 3 datasets, evaluate SAM with: point only, exact box, point + correct-area disk mask prompt, point + randomly-shifted box of correct size, box of wrong size at correct position. Rank the recovered fraction of the point-to-box gap.
main_risk: Mask-prompt pathway may be too weak in SAM to carry the scale signal cleanly, confounding the decomposition.
community_default_belief: Boxes are better prompts because they localize the object more completely; ambiguity is resolved by tighter spatial constraint.
why_that_may_be_wrong: A box constrains area and aspect ratio far more strongly than it constrains which pixels belong to the object; SAM's failure cases under point prompts are dominated by granularity errors, which are scale errors.
fastest_falsification: Half a day: on 100 COCO-style instances, compare point-only vs point+correct-size-wrong-position box; if no gap is recovered, the scale hypothesis dies.

consolidation.territory: T01 SAM / Foundation Model adaptation / PEFT

one_line: SAM's mask output is not shift-stable at sub-patch scale: the same click at different sub-token offsets yields measurably different masks.
problem: [KNOWN FACT] ViT encoders tokenize images into fixed patches (16px for SAM's encoder), and positional encodings are tied to that grid; whether prompt responses inherit grid aliasing is unmeasured.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] SAM exhibits systematic sub-patch aliasing: shifting the entire image (or the click) by 1-15 pixels changes mask boundaries by far more than the shift itself, with error peaking at half-patch offsets.
falsifiable_prediction: Boundary displacement between masks of shifted inputs, after un-shifting, will show a periodic pattern with period equal to patch size; smooth (anti-aliased) downsampling of inputs will reduce the amplitude.
why_important: Aliasing puts a hard floor on boundary accuracy that no PEFT can fix from the decoder side; quantifying it separates 'adaptation problems' from 'architecture-induced noise'.
why_possibly_novel: [VERIFIED PRIOR WORK] Shift-invariance failures are documented for CNN classifiers (anti-aliasing literature); [HYPOTHESIS] a prompt-conditional, mask-level aliasing audit of SAM appears missing.
minimal_falsification_experiment: For 100 images, translate each by 0-16 px in both axes, run SAM with correspondingly translated prompts, un-translate the masks, and measure boundary F-score against the unshifted prediction as a function of offset phase.
main_risk: Effect size may be small relative to SAM's stochastic boundary error, requiring careful separation of aliasing from ambiguity noise.
community_default_belief: SAM's boundary errors are attributed to training data and decoder capacity; input-grid aliasing is not discussed as a failure source in adaptation papers.
why_that_may_be_wrong: Every downstream interpolation (patch embedding, 64x64 feature grid, 4x mask upsampling) compounds grid artifacts; there is no anti-aliasing anywhere in the pipeline.
fastest_falsification: Two hours: 10 images, horizontal shifts 0..16px, plot mean boundary displacement vs offset; a flat curve falsifies.

consolidation.territory: T01 SAM / Foundation Model adaptation / PEFT

one_line: Negative clicks are semantically weaker than positive clicks: they carve along low-level edges, so one negative click in clutter often hurts more than a positive click helps.
problem: Interactive pipelines treat positive and negative clicks as symmetric information, but SAM's training procedure and decoder may not honor that symmetry.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Negative prompts trigger boundary-following exclusion along nearest contrast edges rather than semantic removal, producing over-carving in textured or cluttered regions.
falsifiable_prediction: On cluttered scenes, the expected IoU change of a random informative negative click will be lower (and more often negative) than the IoU change of an equally-informative positive click; the excluded region will align with low-level edge maps rather than object boundaries.
why_important: Interactive segmentation budgets clicks; if negatives are unreliable, annotation UIs and simulated-click training protocols are miscalibrated, and click-simulation evaluations overstate real performance.
why_possibly_novel: [HYPOTHESIS] Sign-asymmetry of prompt information in SAM has not, to our knowledge, been isolated as a measurable defect; interactive-segmentation work predates SAM's specific prompt encoder.
minimal_falsification_experiment: Simulate correction sessions on 500 instances: at matched error mass, apply either the standard positive-click policy or negative-click policy; compare per-click IoU deltas and overlay carved regions with an edge detector output.
main_risk: Click-placement policy choices could dominate the measured asymmetry; needs multiple policies to be conclusive.
community_default_belief: Positive and negative clicks are dual: each click adds roughly one bit of region information, and standard interactive protocols alternate them freely.
why_that_may_be_wrong: SA-1B-style training generates prompts from ground-truth masks where negatives are sampled from backgrounds that are typically homogeneous; cluttered negatives are out-of-distribution for the prompt encoder.
fastest_falsification: Three hours: 50 cluttered images, one round of positive-vs-negative correction each, sign test on IoU deltas.

consolidation.territory: T01 SAM / Foundation Model adaptation / PEFT

one_line: Interactive SAM refinement enters limit cycles: after ~3 clicks, fixing one region reliably breaks another because the decoder has no correction memory.
problem: [KNOWN FACT] SAM conditions on a set of prompts (and optionally a previous mask) but has no explicit state of which errors were already corrected; multi-round behavior is rarely evaluated beyond mean IoU-vs-clicks curves.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] A significant fraction of interactive sessions exhibit non-monotone IoU with oscillation between error modes (mask flips between two attractors), and this fraction grows with object complexity.
falsifiable_prediction: Measuring per-click IoU trajectories will show that beyond 3-5 clicks, the probability of an IoU decrease on the next click rises substantially, and error maps will show recurring spatial alternation rather than steady shrinkage.
why_important: Mean curves hide oscillation; annotation tools built on SAM waste human effort in cycles, and 'clicks-to-target-IoU' metrics understate real cost. Exposing attractor dynamics would change how refinement interfaces are designed and how refinement fine-tuning data is generated.
why_possibly_novel: [HYPOTHESIS] Treating interactive segmentation as a dynamical system with attractors and cycles, rather than a monotone refinement process, appears to be an unexplored analysis frame for SAM.
minimal_falsification_experiment: Run scripted 10-click sessions (standard center-of-largest-error policy) on 1k instances; compute oscillation statistics (sign changes of IoU delta, recurrence of error centroids); stratify by boundary complexity.
main_risk: Oscillation may be an artifact of the click policy rather than the model; must test 2-3 policies including human-recorded sessions if available.
community_default_belief: More clicks monotonically improve SAM masks; published clicks-vs-IoU curves rise smoothly, so refinement is assumed convergent.
why_that_may_be_wrong: Averaged curves can rise while a large minority of sessions oscillate; SAM was trained with limited simulated interaction depth, so deep-refinement states are out-of-distribution.
fastest_falsification: Two hours: 100 sessions, count sessions with 2+ IoU decreases in 10 clicks; near-zero count falsifies.

consolidation.territory: T01 SAM / Foundation Model adaptation / PEFT

one_line: SAM resolves ambiguous prompts by SA-1B mask-frequency priors, not image evidence: its multimask ranking mirrors dataset statistics of mask granularity.
problem: When a click is consistent with several objects/parts, something must break the tie; whether the tiebreaker is image evidence or a learned dataset prior is unknown.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] The ranking among SAM's candidate masks for ambiguous clicks matches the relative frequency of comparable mask granularities in SA-1B, and stays fixed even when image evidence (contrast, closure) is manipulated to favor the alternative.
falsifiable_prediction: Synthetic scenes where low-level evidence is parametrically shifted toward the 'part' interpretation will fail to flip SAM's ranking until extreme values, while a dataset-frequency model predicts the ranking with high accuracy.
why_important: Prior-dominated ambiguity resolution means SAM-based auto-labeling silently imposes SA-1B granularity conventions on every downstream dataset - a contamination channel nobody audits.
why_possibly_novel: [HYPOTHESIS] Connecting multimask ranking to pretraining mask statistics as a measurable prior (rather than describing it qualitatively) appears new.
minimal_falsification_experiment: Build parametric synthetic images (nested shapes with controllable edge strength); estimate SA-1B granularity statistics from its public metadata; compare ranking predictions of a frequency-prior model vs an image-evidence model across the parameter sweep.
main_risk: Public SA-1B statistics may be too coarse to build the frequency prior; would need a proxy prior from a sample of the dataset.
community_default_belief: SAM's top-ranked mask reflects the most visually salient/likely object in that image, i.e., the ranking is evidence-driven.
why_that_may_be_wrong: The IoU-ranking head was trained to predict overlap with SA-1B ground truth; if annotators/auto-masks systematically preferred certain granularities, matching the prior minimizes training loss regardless of evidence.
fastest_falsification: One day: nested-square synthetic sweep; if ranking flips track edge-strength promptly, the prior-dominance claim dies.

consolidation.territory: T01 SAM / Foundation Model adaptation / PEFT

one_line: SAM's 'category-blind' prompt tokens actually acquire semantic content: object class is linearly decodable from decoder cross-attention states.
problem: [KNOWN FACT] SAM is trained without category labels; the community treats its outputs as category-free geometry. Whether category information nonetheless concentrates in the decoder's prompt-token states is untested.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] The decoder's output token embeddings (after cross-attention with image features) carry linearly decodable category information well above what the raw pooled image features at the same location provide.
falsifiable_prediction: A linear probe on SAM decoder output tokens will classify the prompted object's category with accuracy substantially above a probe on location-pooled encoder features, indicating the prompting process itself aggregates semantics.
why_important: If true, 'free' semantics ride along every SAM query, enabling open-vocabulary-ish grouping, better active learning, and a new adaptation surface (probe the tokens instead of tuning weights).
why_possibly_novel: [HYPOTHESIS] Probing SAM's decoder token states (as opposed to encoder features, which have been probed in prior work) for semantics appears unexplored.
minimal_falsification_experiment: On a labeled instance dataset, run SAM with GT-box prompts, harvest decoder output tokens, train linear probes for category, compare with probes on ROI-pooled encoder features and on CLIP features as an upper reference.
main_risk: Semantics in tokens may just re-encode mask shape (shape->category leakage); needs shape-controlled probes.
community_default_belief: SAM is 'semantic-free': it segments anything without knowing what it is, and semantics must be bolted on externally (e.g., pairing with a classifier).
why_that_may_be_wrong: Selecting which pixels belong together requires implicit knowledge of object regularities; the decoder token is the computational bottleneck where that knowledge must concentrate.
fastest_falsification: One day on COCO: token probe vs pooled-feature probe; no advantage for tokens falsifies.

consolidation.territory: T01 SAM / Foundation Model adaptation / PEFT

one_line: When the domain gap is granularity (not appearance), tuning a handful of prompt tokens matches LoRA - adaptation without touching any weight.
problem: PEFT choices for SAM adaptation are made blind to the *type* of domain gap; some gaps may be resolvable purely in prompt space.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] For target domains where oracle prompt/multimask selection already achieves high IoU (gap = wrong default granularity/convention), learning a small set of soft prompt tokens closes most of the gap; LoRA's extra capacity only matters when oracle-prompt IoU is low (gap = appearance).
falsifiable_prediction: Across ~10 domains, the LoRA-minus-prompt-tuning performance gap will correlate strongly and negatively with zero-shot oracle-prompt IoU; domains above an oracle threshold will show near-parity.
why_important: Gives a cheap pre-test (oracle-prompt evaluation) that predicts which adaptation machinery a domain needs, replacing trial-and-error PEFT selection with a diagnostic.
why_possibly_novel: [HYPOTHESIS] A predictive theory of *which* PEFT class a domain needs, based on a measurable gap decomposition, appears absent; papers report method-vs-method tables without gap typing.
minimal_falsification_experiment: Pick 10 datasets spanning medical/industrial/natural; measure zero-shot oracle-prompt IoU; train prompt-token tuning and rank-8 LoRA with matched budgets; test the predicted correlation.
main_risk: Oracle-prompt IoU may be uniformly low across interesting domains, leaving no variance to test the correlation.
community_default_belief: Weight-space PEFT (LoRA/adapters) is the default for SAM adaptation; prompt tuning is regarded as strictly weaker and usually skipped. [VERIFIED PRIOR WORK] LoRA-based SAM adapters (e.g., SAMed-style approaches) dominate the medical adaptation literature.
why_that_may_be_wrong: Much of the measured domain gap may be convention mismatch (what to segment) rather than perception failure (how to segment), and conventions are exactly what prompt tokens can encode.
fastest_falsification: One day: two domains (one high oracle-IoU, one low), prompt tuning vs LoRA; if prompt tuning fails on both, the typing hypothesis is dead.

consolidation.territory: T01 SAM / Foundation Model adaptation / PEFT

one_line: Mask instability under click jitter predicts SAM errors better than SAM's own IoU-prediction head.
problem: [KNOWN FACT] SAM ships an IoU-prediction head used for ranking and quality filtering; its reliability as a per-instance error detector under domain shift is questionable but it remains the default confidence signal.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] The variance of predicted masks under small prompt perturbations (click jitter within the object) is a strictly better failure detector than the IoU head, especially out of domain, because it measures decision-boundary proximity rather than a learned regression that can itself shift.
falsifiable_prediction: Across in-domain and shifted datasets, jitter-variance will achieve higher AUROC for detecting IoU<0.5 failures than the IoU head; the advantage will grow with domain shift.
why_important: Every SAM auto-labeling and active-learning pipeline filters by the IoU head; a better zero-training confidence signal immediately upgrades all of them and changes how 'model self-knowledge' is sourced.
why_possibly_novel: [HYPOTHESIS] Input-sensitivity-based confidence for promptable segmentation, benchmarked head-to-head against the built-in quality head across shift levels, appears unreported.
minimal_falsification_experiment: On 5 datasets at increasing shift from natural images, compute per-instance (a) IoU-head score, (b) mean pairwise IoU across 8 jittered clicks; compare failure-detection AUROC and risk-coverage curves.
main_risk: 8x inference cost; also jitter policy (radius) may need per-domain tuning, weakening the 'zero-training' claim.
community_default_belief: The IoU head is treated as SAM's calibrated quality estimate and is used directly for mask filtering in auto-annotation pipelines.
why_that_may_be_wrong: The IoU head is a learned function of the same features that cause the errors - it fails jointly with the mask under shift, whereas input-sensitivity does not rely on any quality-specific training.
fastest_falsification: Three hours: one shifted dataset, 300 instances, compare AUROCs.

consolidation.territory: T01 SAM / Foundation Model adaptation / PEFT

one_line: Everything-mode grid prompting has a computable blind spot: objects thinner than the grid pitch are missed at rates predicted by pure geometry.
problem: [KNOWN FACT] SAM's automatic mask generation prompts a regular point grid and post-filters; recall for thin/elongated structures in this mode is anecdotally poor but not systematically attributed.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Everything-mode recall for an object is well predicted by the probability that a grid point lands inside it (a closed-form function of its area and shape), meaning the failure is a sampling artifact, not a perception failure.
falsifiable_prediction: Plotting recall vs the geometric hit-probability across object shapes will collapse curves from different datasets onto one function; conditioning on 'at least one grid point inside' will show near-normal segmentation quality for thin objects.
why_important: Distinguishes sampling failure from model failure for a widely used mode; implies cheap fixes (edge-biased or stratified prompting) and warns that datasets auto-labeled in everything mode systematically lack thin structures - a bias that propagates into every model trained on them.
why_possibly_novel: [HYPOTHESIS] A quantitative sampling-theory account of everything-mode recall appears unwritten; complaints about thin structures are usually attributed to the model itself.
minimal_falsification_experiment: On datasets with thin structures (cracks, wires, vessels), compute per-instance grid hit-probability, measure everything-mode recall, and compare conditional quality given a hit vs point-prompted quality.
main_risk: NMS and post-filtering thresholds add non-geometric loss that must be carefully ablated.
community_default_belief: SAM 'cannot segment thin structures' - the deficiency is attributed to the encoder/decoder, motivating architectural fixes and high-res variants. [VERIFIED PRIOR WORK] HQ-SAM-style work targets fine-structure quality.
why_that_may_be_wrong: Thin-structure recall failures in everything mode confound sampling geometry with model capacity; conditioning on prompt hits may reveal the model was never asked.
fastest_falsification: Two hours: crack dataset, recall-vs-hit-probability plot plus prompted-quality check on missed instances.

consolidation.territory: T01 SAM / Foundation Model adaptation / PEFT

one_line: Where LoRA lands tells you what shifted: appearance shifts concentrate updates in early-layer V/O projections, convention shifts in late-layer Q/K - a readable signature of domain-gap type.
problem: LoRA is applied uniformly to attention projections with no theory of which projections encode which kind of adaptation; the learned updates are discarded as uninterpretable.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] The distribution of LoRA update energy across (layer depth x projection type) is a stable, interpretable signature: photometric/sensor shifts load early V/O; label-convention/granularity shifts load late Q/K and decoder cross-attention.
falsifiable_prediction: Training LoRA on synthetic shifts of known type (pure photometric vs pure label-restyle of the same images) will produce separable energy signatures, and a classifier on signatures will predict shift type of natural domains that can then be verified by targeted interventions.
why_important: Turns PEFT from a black box into a measurement instrument for diagnosing domain gaps, informing where to spend capacity and what data to collect.
why_possibly_novel: [HYPOTHESIS] Using the *location* of PEFT updates as a diagnostic readout of shift type (rather than optimizing placement for accuracy) appears to be an unexplored inversion.
minimal_falsification_experiment: Construct controlled shifts on one dataset: (a) stain/color transform with identical labels, (b) identical images with dilated/eroded labels; train identical LoRA configs; compare per-layer/per-projection update norms and subspace angles across 3 seeds.
main_risk: Update location may be dominated by optimization dynamics (layer-wise gradient scale) rather than shift semantics, washing out the signature.
community_default_belief: LoRA placement is a hyperparameter chosen by ablation (usually 'all attention layers works best'); the learned updates themselves carry no interpretable structure worth reading.
why_that_may_be_wrong: Gradient flow concentrates updates where loss reduction is available; if different shift types create loss at different computational stages, the update geography must reflect it.
fastest_falsification: One day: the two synthetic shifts, three seeds each; overlapping signatures falsify.

consolidation.territory: T01 SAM / Foundation Model adaptation / PEFT

one_line: Learned LoRA updates have an effective rank that saturates far below the allocated rank, and that saturation value is a transferable 'intrinsic rank' of the task.
problem: Rank is the main LoRA hyperparameter, tuned by grid search per task; there is no measured task property that predicts it.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] For SAM adaptation, the stable rank of the converged update B*A saturates as allocated rank grows, and the saturation value (a) predicts the minimal allocated rank achieving full accuracy, and (b) is consistent across LoRA variants and seeds - i.e., it is a property of the task, not the method.
falsifiable_prediction: Across 8 domains, minimal sufficient allocated rank will correlate strongly with measured saturation stable-rank; tasks with equal accuracy but different measured intrinsic rank will respond differently to rank cuts.
why_important: Converts rank selection from grid search to measurement, and gives a quantitative footing to 'task complexity' for adaptation - useful for budgeting across many deployed domains.
why_possibly_novel: [VERIFIED PRIOR WORK] Intrinsic-dimensionality analyses exist for full fine-tuning in NLP; [HYPOTHESIS] a saturation-based, cross-method-stable intrinsic rank for promptable segmentation adaptation appears unmeasured.
minimal_falsification_experiment: Train LoRA at ranks {4,16,64,256} on 8 domains x 3 seeds; compute stable rank of converged updates per layer; test whether rank-{saturation} predicts the accuracy-vs-allocated-rank knee.
main_risk: Stable rank may keep growing with allocated rank (no saturation), or vary wildly across layers, preventing a single task-level number.
community_default_belief: Rank is a capacity dial: more rank = more capacity = risk of overfitting; choose by validation. No task-intrinsic quantity is assumed measurable.
why_that_may_be_wrong: If the needed update lives in a low-dimensional subspace determined by the domain gap, optimization should find it regardless of allocation, leaving measurable spectral fingerprints.
fastest_falsification: One day: 2 domains, ranks {8,128}; if stable rank tracks allocated rank linearly, saturation fails.

consolidation.territory: T01 SAM / Foundation Model adaptation / PEFT

one_line: Low-rank LoRA outcomes are an initialization lottery: the random init of A biases which solution subspace is found, making per-seed variance a capacity issue, not noise.
problem: [KNOWN FACT] Standard LoRA initializes B to zero and A randomly, so early training explores only directions in A's random row space. The consequence for solution diversity at low rank is uncharacterized for vision adaptation.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] At low rank, the converged update subspace retains substantial overlap with the *initial* random subspace of A (it never fully rotates away), so different seeds converge to genuinely different functions - explaining why low-rank results have higher seed variance and why LoRA soups help.
falsifiable_prediction: Principal angles between converged update subspaces of different seeds will be large at rank 4 and shrink with rank; overlap between converged and initial A subspaces will exceed random-baseline overlap; per-seed error sets (which instances fail) will differ more at low rank.
why_important: Reframes low-rank instability as an exploration limit with concrete fixes (re-initialization schedules, subspace annealing) and warns that single-seed LoRA comparisons at low rank are statistically meaningless.
why_possibly_novel: [HYPOTHESIS] The persistence of the initialization subspace in converged LoRA updates appears unquantified in the vision-adaptation setting.
minimal_falsification_experiment: Rank {4,64} x 5 seeds on 2 SAM adaptation tasks; measure principal angles (init vs converged; seed vs seed), per-instance error overlap, and soup gains as a function of rank.
main_risk: Long training may fully rotate the subspace even at low rank, leaving only trivial overlap.
community_default_belief: Seed variance in LoRA results is generic SGD noise; init details are irrelevant because B=0 makes the start function-preserving.
why_that_may_be_wrong: Function-preserving is not exploration-neutral: gradients to A are gated through B (and vice versa), so the reachable set early in training is anchored to A's random subspace at exactly the ranks where there is no room to escape.
fastest_falsification: Six hours: rank-4, 5 seeds, one task; small principal angles between seeds falsify.

consolidation.territory: T01 SAM / Foundation Model adaptation / PEFT

one_line: PEFT doesn't build new circuits, it re-weights old ones: attention-head ablations transfer between the frozen and LoRA-adapted SAM almost unchanged.
problem: Whether adaptation adds computation or re-routes existing computation is a basic mechanistic question with no answer for vision foundation models.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] After LoRA adaptation of SAM to a new domain, the causal importance profile of attention heads (measured by ablation damage) is nearly unchanged - adaptation amplifies/reweights existing pathways rather than creating new ones.
falsifiable_prediction: Head-ablation damage vectors before/after adaptation will correlate above 0.9; heads unimportant pre-adaptation will remain unimportant; contrast case: training the same LoRA on a *task change* (e.g., inverted labels) will break the correlation.
why_important: If PEFT is pathway-reweighting, then (a) pre-adaptation head profiling predicts adaptability, (b) forgetting must occur via shared-pathway interference - both actionable; if falsified, PEFT genuinely constructs new computation with tiny parameter budgets, which is mechanistically remarkable.
why_possibly_novel: [HYPOTHESIS] Circuit-level invariance testing across PEFT for promptable segmentation appears undone; mechanistic work concentrates on language models.
minimal_falsification_experiment: On 2 adaptation domains: ablate each encoder/decoder attention head individually in frozen and adapted models, measure per-head IoU damage on target data, compare profiles; include the label-inversion control.
main_risk: Head ablation is a coarse causal probe; distributed circuit changes could hide below its resolution.
community_default_belief: PEFT 'learns the task' - implicitly assumed to encode new domain-specific computation in the adapters.
why_that_may_be_wrong: Rank-limited additive updates mathematically favor rescaling existing feature directions; truly new computation may require rank and nonlinearity PEFT doesn't have.
fastest_falsification: One day: one domain, head-damage correlation pre/post; correlation < 0.5 falsifies immediately.

consolidation.territory: T01 SAM / Foundation Model adaptation / PEFT

one_line: For sensor-modality shifts (thermal, ultrasound, fluorescence), adapting only the patch embedding plus first ViT block matches full-depth LoRA - the cross-modal gap lives in the first-layer statistics.
problem: PEFT for cross-modal SAM transfer spreads capacity across all layers by default; where the modality gap actually resides is unlocalized.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Modality shifts are overwhelmingly a first-layer problem: once token statistics are renormalized to natural-image-like distributions, frozen deeper layers process the new modality adequately.
falsifiable_prediction: Patch-embed+block-1 adaptation will reach >=90% of all-layer LoRA's gain on modality-shift domains but a much lower share on label-convention domains; feature-distribution distance to natural images (per layer) will collapse after layer 1 in adapted models.
why_important: Cuts adaptation cost and, more importantly, tests a clean scientific claim about where modality-invariance emerges in vision transformers - with consequences for how future encoders should be pretrained (modality-agnostic stems).
why_possibly_novel: [HYPOTHESIS] Depth-localization of the cross-modal gap for SAM via matched-budget placement experiments appears unreported; existing adapter papers place capacity everywhere.
minimal_falsification_experiment: Three modality-shift datasets + two convention-shift controls; compare (a) first-block-only, (b) last-block-only, (c) uniform LoRA at matched trainable parameters; measure per-layer CKA to natural-image features.
main_risk: Ultrasound/thermal gaps may include mid-level texture semantics that first-layer renormalization cannot express.
community_default_belief: Deeper layers must adapt because 'semantic' domain differences live there; uniform or late-layer placement is standard practice.
why_that_may_be_wrong: ViT features are heavily shaped by token input statistics; a distribution mismatch at the stem corrupts all downstream layers in ways that look 'deep' but originate shallow.
fastest_falsification: Six hours: one thermal dataset, first-block-only vs uniform LoRA at matched params.

consolidation.territory: T01 SAM / Foundation Model adaptation / PEFT

one_line: LayerNorm-affine-only tuning suffices for a large class of SAM domain shifts because domain gaps act multiplicatively on channel statistics.
problem: The minimal sufficient parameterization for SAM domain adaptation is unknown; LoRA may be overkill for shifts that are channel-wise rescalings.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] For photometric/stain/sensor-gain shifts, tuning only LayerNorm scales and biases (a few thousand parameters) recovers most of LoRA's gain, because these shifts manifest as channel-wise mean/variance displacement of features.
falsifiable_prediction: LN-only tuning will reach a high fraction of rank-8 LoRA performance on photometric-shift domains and a low fraction on structural-shift domains; measured per-channel feature-moment displacement will predict which regime a domain is in.
why_important: Establishes a two-regime taxonomy of domain shift with a cheap diagnostic and a near-zero-parameter fix for one regime; also probes what 'domain' means at the feature level.
why_possibly_novel: [VERIFIED PRIOR WORK] Bias-only (BitFit) and normalization-tuning have precedents in NLP/classification; [HYPOTHESIS] using moment-displacement measurements to *predict* LN-tuning sufficiency for promptable segmentation appears new.
minimal_falsification_experiment: Six domains spanning photometric and structural shifts; train LN-only vs LoRA; separately measure per-channel moment shifts of frozen features; test the predicted regime split.
main_risk: SAM's ViT may distribute domain response across token interactions in ways channel moments don't capture, blurring the regimes.
community_default_belief: Meaningful adaptation requires updating weight matrices (low-rank or adapters); normalization tuning is a weak baseline usually omitted for segmentation.
why_that_may_be_wrong: Segmentation quality depends heavily on feature magnitude calibration for boundary decisions; multiplicative repair may be exactly the needed operation for many real shifts.
fastest_falsification: Four hours: one stain-shift dataset, LN-only vs LoRA.

consolidation.territory: T01 SAM / Foundation Model adaptation / PEFT

one_line: Label-convention gaps do NOT live in the decoder: decoder-only LoRA fails to absorb label-style shifts that encoder LoRA absorbs easily.
problem: It is intuitively assumed that 'what to segment' (label convention) is a decoder-level decision in SAM, so cheap decoder-only tuning should fix convention gaps; this assumption is untested.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Convention changes (e.g., include-holes vs exclude-holes, instance vs semantic grouping) require encoder feature changes because grouping evidence is computed in the encoder; the decoder is a readout too weak to re-group.
falsifiable_prediction: On same-image different-convention benchmarks (relabelings of one dataset), decoder-only LoRA will plateau well below encoder-only LoRA at matched parameters, and the gap will be largest for conventions requiring long-range regrouping.
why_important: Decoder-only tuning is popular for cost reasons; if conventions live upstream, this practice silently caps achievable quality, and 'lightweight task heads' inherit a wrong mental model of where task semantics reside.
why_possibly_novel: [HYPOTHESIS] Same-image relabeling as a controlled probe of encoder-vs-decoder responsibility for label semantics in SAM appears unexplored.
minimal_falsification_experiment: Create two convention variants of one dataset (systematic relabel rules); train decoder-only vs encoder-only vs full LoRA at matched budgets; measure plateau gaps by convention type.
main_risk: Result may depend on SAM's specific decoder capacity; a slightly larger decoder head could flip conclusions (should include one control).
community_default_belief: Encoder = generic perception, decoder = task convention; adapting the small decoder is the parameter-efficient way to change what gets segmented.
why_that_may_be_wrong: SAM's decoder is a thin two-way transformer over precomputed features - if grouping structure isn't already in the features, no cheap readout can create it.
fastest_falsification: Six hours: one relabeled dataset pair, decoder-only vs encoder-only LoRA.

consolidation.territory: T01 SAM / Foundation Model adaptation / PEFT

one_line: PEFT trains stably at high learning rates because low-rank projection filters gradient conflict: per-image gradients agree more inside the LoRA subspace than in full weight space.
problem: LoRA is empirically robust to learning-rate choice relative to full fine-tuning, but the mechanism is unexplained folklore.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Projecting gradients through a low-rank bottleneck suppresses high-variance conflicting components, raising per-batch gradient cosine similarity; PEFT's optimization stability is a variance-reduction effect, not a capacity effect.
falsifiable_prediction: Measured pairwise cosine similarity of per-image gradients will be systematically higher for LoRA parameters than for the corresponding full-matrix gradients; artificially projecting full-FT gradients onto random low-rank subspaces will reproduce much of the stability.
why_important: Explains when PEFT should NOT be stable (tasks whose consistent gradient direction is high-rank) and suggests optimizer designs (rank-filtered updates) that decouple stability from parameter savings.
why_possibly_novel: [HYPOTHESIS] A gradient-conflict account of PEFT optimization stability, tested on vision adaptation, appears unarticulated; existing explanations invoke 'fewer parameters' loosely.
minimal_falsification_experiment: During SAM adaptation, log per-image gradient cosines in (a) LoRA space, (b) full space, (c) random low-rank projections of full space; correlate with maximal stable LR found by LR range tests.
main_risk: Gradient cosine statistics may be dominated by layer scale effects requiring careful normalization to interpret.
community_default_belief: PEFT is stable because it has fewer parameters and stays near the pretrained point; stability is framed as a regularization side effect.
why_that_may_be_wrong: Parameter count per se doesn't control gradient noise geometry; projection does - random-subspace controls can dissociate the two explanations.
fastest_falsification: Four hours: log cosines for LoRA vs full gradients on one task; no difference falsifies.

consolidation.territory: T01 SAM / Foundation Model adaptation / PEFT

one_line: 'Low rank prevents overfitting' is a myth of missing regularization: spectrally-regularized rank-64 LoRA never loses to rank-4 on small SAM adaptation sets.
problem: Practitioners cap rank on small datasets citing overfitting; whether rank itself, or absent spectral control, causes the overfitting is unresolved.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Overfitting attributed to high rank is caused by unregularized singular-value growth; with nuclear-norm or spectral weight decay on B*A, high-rank LoRA weakly dominates low-rank across data scales (it can always emulate low rank).
falsifiable_prediction: On few-shot SAM adaptation (10-100 images), regularized rank-64 will match or beat the best of {rank-4, rank-8} on every domain tested, eliminating the rank-vs-data-size interaction reported anecdotally.
why_important: Removes one hyperparameter from every deployment and clarifies the actual regularizer at work in PEFT - relevant far beyond SAM.
why_possibly_novel: [HYPOTHESIS] Direct spectral-regularization-vs-rank-capping equivalence tests for vision-foundation PEFT appear unpublished; rank sweeps typically hold regularization fixed.
minimal_falsification_experiment: 4 domains x {10,30,100} training images x ranks {4,64,64+spectral-reg} x 3 seeds; compare test IoU; check whether regularized-64 ever loses beyond seed noise.
main_risk: Choosing the spectral penalty strength fairly (without per-task tuning advantage) requires a principled protocol.
community_default_belief: Small data demands small rank; rank is the primary capacity control for LoRA and must be matched to dataset size.
why_that_may_be_wrong: Rank caps the update subspace dimension but not its magnitude; generalization theory points to norms, not dimensions, as the binding constraint in overparameterized regimes.
fastest_falsification: Six hours: one 30-image domain, the three configurations.

consolidation.territory: T01 SAM / Foundation Model adaptation / PEFT

one_line: The right LoRA rank is measurable before training: the spectral dimensionality of the source-target feature discrepancy predicts the accuracy-vs-rank knee.
problem: Rank selection requires training multiple models; no pre-training measurement is known to predict it.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] The number of significant components in the frozen-feature discrepancy between source-like and target data (e.g., eigen-spectrum of the mean-shift + covariance-mismatch operator per layer) linearly predicts the minimal LoRA rank achieving near-max accuracy.
falsifiable_prediction: Across >=10 domains, a spectral gap-dimension measured from ~100 unlabeled target images will predict the rank knee with rank-correlation >0.8; domains with equal gap magnitude but different gap dimension will need different ranks as predicted.
why_important: Zero-training hyperparameter prediction from unlabeled data would make large-scale multi-domain deployment (hundreds of LoRAs) tractable and provides a quantitative bridge between distribution-shift geometry and adaptation capacity.
why_possibly_novel: [HYPOTHESIS] Predicting PEFT capacity needs from unlabeled feature-space measurements appears unaddressed; existing rank studies are post-hoc sweeps.
minimal_falsification_experiment: 10 domains: measure per-layer feature discrepancy spectra with frozen SAM; train rank sweep {2..128}; locate knees; test the predictive correlation and its robustness to the number of unlabeled images.
main_risk: The rank knee may be governed by label-space (convention) complexity invisible to unlabeled feature statistics.
community_default_belief: Rank must be found empirically per task; unlabeled target data can estimate gap size but not the capacity required to close it.
why_that_may_be_wrong: If LoRA updates primarily realign feature subspaces (a linear operation), the dimensionality of the misalignment should directly set required rank - a testable linear-algebraic link.
fastest_falsification: One day: 3 domains, spectra + coarse rank sweep {4,16,64}; wrong ordering falsifies early.

consolidation.territory: T01 SAM / Foundation Model adaptation / PEFT

one_line: Domain-LoRA arithmetic works only under subspace disjointness: interference when merging SAM LoRAs is predicted by per-layer principal-angle overlap between updates.
problem: [VERIFIED PRIOR WORK] Task-arithmetic/model-merging literature shows adapters sometimes compose additively and sometimes interfere; for SAM domain adapters there is no predictive rule for when merging is safe.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Additive merging of two domain LoRAs preserves both domains' performance iff their update subspaces are near-orthogonal per layer; the performance drop under merging is a monotone function of a single overlap statistic computable without any evaluation data.
falsifiable_prediction: Across many LoRA pairs, merged-model degradation will correlate strongly with the overlap statistic; artificially orthogonalized training (penalizing overlap with a fixed reference subspace) will yield mergeable adapters at small solo-accuracy cost.
why_important: Multi-domain SAM deployment wants one merged model instead of adapter switching; a data-free mergeability certificate makes composition an engineering decision rather than trial and error, and tests whether 'domains' occupy separable weight-space directions at all.
why_possibly_novel: [HYPOTHESIS] A quantitative, pre-evaluation interference predictor for segmentation-domain adapters appears missing; merging papers report outcomes, not certificates.
minimal_falsification_experiment: Train LoRAs on 6 domains; evaluate all 15 pairwise merges; regress degradation on per-layer principal-angle overlap; then train 2 orthogonality-constrained LoRAs and verify improved mergeability.
main_risk: Interference may be governed by activation-space overlap (which inputs excite the updates) rather than weight-space overlap, requiring a different statistic.
community_default_belief: Adapter merging is hit-or-miss; practitioners either keep adapters separate or accept averaged-model degradation as unpredictable.
why_that_may_be_wrong: For linear additive updates, superposition theory says interference must be a function of subspace geometry; nobody has checked whether the simple geometric statistic already suffices in practice.
fastest_falsification: One day: 3 domains, 3 merges, plot degradation vs overlap; zero correlation falsifies.

consolidation.territory: T01 SAM / Foundation Model adaptation / PEFT

one_line: Domain fine-tuning collapses SAM's ambiguity machinery: after LoRA on one domain, the three multimask outputs become near-duplicates even on natural images.
problem: Adaptation papers measure target-domain IoU and sometimes source-domain IoU, but never whether SAM's signature capability - representing segmentation ambiguity via diverse candidates - survives.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Single-domain fine-tuning (which usually has one 'correct' granularity) collapses multimask diversity globally, not just in-domain: mean pairwise IoU among the three outputs rises sharply everywhere, destroying part/whole option coverage.
falsifiable_prediction: On held-out natural images, multimask pairwise IoU will increase substantially after domain LoRA, and oracle-selection gains (best-of-3 minus top-1) will shrink toward zero; the effect will scale with training epochs and inversely with prompt diversity in the fine-tuning data.
why_important: Ambiguity representation is what makes SAM useful for interactive tools and label auditing; losing it silently makes adapted checkpoints unfit for those uses - a capability regression no current benchmark detects.
why_possibly_novel: [HYPOTHESIS] Multimask-diversity collapse as a measurable forgetting axis (distinct from IoU forgetting) appears unproposed.
minimal_falsification_experiment: Fine-tune LoRA on one medical dataset; before/after, measure multimask pairwise IoU and best-of-3 oracle gain on a fixed natural-image probe set with ambiguous clicks; sweep epochs.
main_risk: Collapse may be trivially fixable with multimask-preserving losses, making it a transient observation rather than a durable phenomenon (though that fix would itself be a contribution).
community_default_belief: Forgetting from PEFT is mild and measured as source-domain IoU drop; if source IoU holds, the checkpoint is considered safe.
why_that_may_be_wrong: IoU of the top mask can be preserved while the distribution over interpretations collapses; the loss functions used in adaptation actively penalize diversity because targets are single masks.
fastest_falsification: Three hours: one adapted checkpoint vs base, 200 ambiguous clicks, compare pairwise-IoU histograms.

consolidation.territory: T01 SAM / Foundation Model adaptation / PEFT

one_line: Calibration dies before accuracy: PEFT wrecks SAM's IoU-head reliability on the source domain long before source-domain mask quality drops.
problem: Forgetting is monitored via mask accuracy; the reliability of the model's self-assessment (the IoU-prediction head) under adaptation is unmonitored.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] The IoU head's calibration (error of predicted vs actual IoU) on source-domain data degrades much faster during PEFT than source-domain mask IoU itself - self-knowledge is the most fragile capability.
falsifiable_prediction: Tracking both metrics across fine-tuning steps will show calibration error inflecting upward several times earlier (in steps) than mask IoU; the effect persists even when the IoU head is frozen (because its input features shift under it).
why_important: Pipelines that filter pseudo-labels or route instances by predicted IoU will silently break after adaptation while looking fine on accuracy dashboards; establishes 'calibration half-life' as a needed reporting metric for adapted checkpoints.
why_possibly_novel: [HYPOTHESIS] The differential fragility of self-assessment vs task performance under PEFT appears unmeasured for segmentation foundation models.
minimal_falsification_experiment: During LoRA adaptation on 2 domains, checkpoint every N steps; on a fixed source probe set, log mask IoU and IoU-head calibration error; compare degradation onset times; repeat with IoU head frozen vs trainable.
main_risk: Onset-time comparison requires defining comparable degradation thresholds for two different metrics - needs care to avoid arbitrary conclusions.
community_default_belief: If source accuracy is preserved, the adapted model is backward-compatible; confidence outputs are an afterthought assumed to degrade in proportion to accuracy.
why_that_may_be_wrong: The IoU head is a regression on features being actively repurposed by the adapter; regression targets are more sensitive to feature drift than argmax-like mask decisions.
fastest_falsification: Six hours: one adaptation run with dense checkpoints, two curves; proportional degradation falsifies.

consolidation.territory: T01 SAM / Foundation Model adaptation / PEFT

one_line: PEFT forgetting is interference-by-similarity, not distance: the natural-image categories most damaged by medical adaptation are those most feature-similar to the medical domain.
problem: Zero-shot degradation after adaptation is reported as a scalar; its structure over categories is unexamined, leaving the mechanism of PEFT forgetting unknown.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Forgetting is concentrated on source categories whose frozen-feature statistics are CLOSEST to the target domain (they share the pathways being rewritten), contradicting the intuition that 'far' capabilities are unaffected and 'near' ones benefit.
falsifiable_prediction: Per-category zero-shot IoU drop after adaptation will correlate positively with feature-space similarity between that category and the target domain; categories in orthogonal feature regions will be nearly untouched regardless of semantic relation.
why_important: A similarity-structured forgetting law enables prediction of collateral damage before deployment (compute similarity, flag at-risk categories) and constrains theories of where domain knowledge is stored in shared weights.
why_possibly_novel: [HYPOTHESIS] Forgetting-vs-similarity structure has been discussed for classification continual learning; testing it for promptable segmentation with feature-similarity as the predictor variable appears new.
minimal_falsification_experiment: Adapt SAM to 2 medical domains; measure per-category zero-shot IoU delta on a broad natural benchmark; regress deltas on encoder-feature similarity (class centroid cosine / CKA) to the target domain; check sign and strength.
main_risk: Per-category IoU deltas are noisy; needs enough instances per category to resolve the correlation.
community_default_belief: Forgetting hits capabilities 'far' from the new task or is roughly uniform; adapting to X is assumed safe for unrelated Y.
why_that_may_be_wrong: Gradient updates flow through the features the target data activates; source categories sharing those features receive the largest uninvited updates - proximity is exposure.
fastest_falsification: Four hours with a public medical-adapted SAM: per-category deltas vs similarity scatter plot.

consolidation.territory: T01 SAM / Foundation Model adaptation / PEFT

one_line: Coarse-label fine-tuning teaches SAM to be sloppy everywhere: boundary precision degrades globally while region IoU is preserved - two separable knowledge stores.
problem: Many adaptation datasets have loose polygon labels; what this label coarseness does to SAM's boundary behavior outside the domain is unmeasured.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Boundary precision and region correctness are stored separably: fine-tuning on coarse labels selectively overwrites the boundary-precision store (hypothesized to live in the upsampling path and early decoder), degrading boundary-F on ALL domains while region IoU is unaffected.
falsifiable_prediction: After fine-tuning on deliberately dilated/simplified labels, natural-image boundary-F will drop significantly with flat region-IoU; restricting PEFT to exclude the mask-upsampling path will protect boundary-F at some cost to fitting the coarse labels.
why_important: Label coarseness is endemic; if it causes global boundary damage, dataset quality requirements for adaptation change, and 'which submodule stores boundary skill' becomes a mappable question.
why_possibly_novel: [HYPOTHESIS] Treating boundary precision as a localizable, independently-forgettable capability appears untested; forgetting is normally reported as a single IoU number.
minimal_falsification_experiment: Take one dataset; make label variants (exact, dilated-5px, polygon-simplified); fine-tune identically; report region IoU and boundary-F on source-domain and natural probes; ablate which adapted submodules carry the sloppiness.
main_risk: Boundary-F degradation may saturate quickly, making dose-response hard to measure.
community_default_belief: Fine-tuning quality tracks label quality only in-domain; out-of-domain behavior is protected by the frozen backbone; region and boundary quality move together.
why_that_may_be_wrong: The decoder/upsampler is small and shared; it is the cheapest place for SGD to encode 'boundaries are approximate', and it is applied to every future prediction.
fastest_falsification: Six hours: exact vs dilated labels, one domain, boundary-F on a fixed natural probe set.

consolidation.territory: T01 SAM / Foundation Model adaptation / PEFT

one_line: PEFT forgetting is displacement, not erasure: 50 rehearsal images restore most zero-shot loss, implying the knowledge is intact but de-routed.
problem: Whether adaptation-induced forgetting destroys information or merely re-biases routing determines the right mitigation, but the question isn't posed for segmentation PEFT.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] After domain LoRA, a tiny rehearsal phase (tens of generic images with diverse prompts, few steps, adapter-only updates) recovers the majority of zero-shot degradation while keeping target-domain gains - indicating shallow displacement.
falsifiable_prediction: Recovery fraction from 50-image rehearsal will exceed 70% of lost zero-shot IoU across domains; recovery speed (steps to plateau) will be far faster than original adaptation, and interleaving 5% rehearsal data during adaptation will prevent most forgetting at negligible target cost.
why_important: If forgetting is cheap to undo, the field's forgetting-mitigation machinery (orthogonal constraints, regularizers) may be overengineering; also probes the storage/routing distinction in foundation-model knowledge.
why_possibly_novel: [VERIFIED PRIOR WORK] Rehearsal is a classic continual-learning tool; [HYPOTHESIS] measuring recovery *asymmetry* (speed and data-cost of un-forgetting vs learning) as evidence about storage-vs-routing in SAM appears new.
minimal_falsification_experiment: 3 adaptation domains; measure zero-shot loss; rehearse with {10,50,200} generic images; report recovery fraction, target retention, and steps-to-recovery vs steps-to-adapt.
main_risk: 'Generic images' choice may drive results; needs a fixed public probe/rehearsal protocol to be reproducible.
community_default_belief: Forgetting must be prevented during training (via constraints/regularization); post-hoc recovery is assumed to trade off directly against target performance.
why_that_may_be_wrong: Low-rank updates can only tilt the function slightly; the pretrained basin is adjacent, so a weak restoring force may suffice - a geometric argument nobody has cashed out empirically for SAM.
fastest_falsification: Six hours: one domain, 50-image rehearsal; recovery <30% with target loss falsifies.

consolidation.territory: T01 SAM / Foundation Model adaptation / PEFT

one_line: Single-prompt fine-tuning kills multi-click repair: adapted SAM loses the ability to integrate correction clicks even in its new specialty domain.
problem: Adaptation recipes overwhelmingly train with one prompt per mask (a box or a point); the interactive-refinement capability this may destroy is never evaluated.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] SAM's ability to use 2nd..kth corrective clicks is a distinct skill maintained only if training includes iterative prompts; single-prompt fine-tuning degrades click-integration so much that in-domain interactive performance of the adapted model falls below the un-adapted base after 3+ clicks.
falsifiable_prediction: IoU-vs-clicks curves: adapted model starts higher (better click-1) but flattens; base SAM crosses over by click 3-5 on the SAME target domain; adding simulated iterative prompts to fine-tuning removes the crossover.
why_important: Medical/industrial users adopt adapted SAMs precisely for human-in-the-loop use; a hidden crossover means the 'better' model is worse in the intended workflow - an evaluation blind spot with direct practical stakes.
why_possibly_novel: [HYPOTHESIS] The click-integration-forgetting effect and its crossover signature appear undocumented; adaptation papers report single-prompt metrics.
minimal_falsification_experiment: Fine-tune with single-box protocol on one medical set; evaluate base vs adapted with a standard simulated-click protocol to 10 clicks; look for crossover; repeat with iterative-prompt fine-tuning.
main_risk: Click simulation policy may favor one model; use 2 policies and report both.
community_default_belief: An adapted model that wins at 1 prompt is assumed better at any number of prompts; interactive capability is treated as automatically inherited from SAM's pretraining.
why_that_may_be_wrong: Correction-integration is conditional behavior on prompt-history distributions absent from single-prompt fine-tuning; distribution shift in prompt space causes forgetting exactly like image-space shift does.
fastest_falsification: Four hours: any public single-prompt-adapted SAM vs base, 10-click curves on its own target data.

consolidation.territory: T01 SAM / Foundation Model adaptation / PEFT

one_line: Adaptation makes SAM texture-greedy: fine-tuning on homogeneous-texture domains measurably shifts SAM's shape-vs-texture reliance, predictable from target-set texture statistics.
problem: [VERIFIED PRIOR WORK] Shape-vs-texture cue-conflict methodology exists for classifiers (Geirhos-style); the cue-reliance drift of segmentation foundation models under adaptation is unmeasured.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] PEFT shifts SAM's grouping cues toward whatever cue-dimension has lowest variance in the target set (often texture in medical/industrial data), and the shift magnitude is predictable from a texture-homogeneity statistic of the training set.
falsifiable_prediction: On segmentation cue-conflict stimuli (shape of A, texture of B), the fraction of texture-consistent masks will increase after adaptation, with cross-domain differences tracking the homogeneity statistic; shape-diverse augmentation will cancel the drift.
why_important: Cue drift predicts brittle deployment (fails when target texture varies) and gives dataset designers a measurable pre-training knob; extends cue-conflict science from classification to promptable grouping.
why_possibly_novel: [HYPOTHESIS] Cue-conflict evaluation adapted to promptable segmentation (which cue wins the grouping, not the label) appears unbuilt.
minimal_falsification_experiment: Build 200 cue-conflict images via texture transfer between shape donors; evaluate base and 4 adapted SAMs; correlate texture-win-rate change with training-set texture homogeneity (e.g., mean pairwise Gram distance).
main_risk: Constructing valid cue-conflict stimuli for segmentation (where 'texture region' must be maskable) is methodologically delicate.
community_default_belief: PEFT learns 'the domain' as a whole; what low-level cue the adapted model now relies on is not a question practitioners ask.
why_that_may_be_wrong: SGD finds the cheapest separating cue; in narrow domains that is typically texture, and low-rank updates are enough to re-weight cue reliance without any architectural change.
fastest_falsification: One day including stimulus construction; no drift on any adapted checkpoint falsifies.

consolidation.territory: T01 SAM / Foundation Model adaptation / PEFT

one_line: 'LoRA learns less but forgets less' has a crossover: when the required update is high-rank, LoRA both underfits the target AND forgets more per unit of target gain than full fine-tuning.
problem: [VERIFIED PRIOR WORK] LLM-focused work reports LoRA forgets less than full fine-tuning while learning less. Whether this tradeoff is universal or breaks on high-rank tasks is untested in vision.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Forgetting-per-target-gain is the right exchange rate, and LoRA's advantage on it inverts for target domains requiring high-rank updates: forced through a narrow subspace, LoRA overdrives shared directions, causing MORE collateral damage per point of target improvement.
falsifiable_prediction: Constructing target tasks with controllable required-rank (e.g., number of independent label-convention changes) will show LoRA's forgetting-per-gain rising with required rank and crossing full FT's; at the crossover, measured update spectra will show LoRA saturating its allocation.
why_important: Breaks a comfortable heuristic ('PEFT is always the safe choice') with a predictive criterion for when it is the risky choice; introduces forgetting-per-gain as the metric adaptation papers should report.
why_possibly_novel: [HYPOTHESIS] The predicted inversion regime and the controllable-rank task construction appear new; existing comparisons use natural tasks with unknown required rank.
minimal_falsification_experiment: Design 4 target tasks of increasing convention-count on one image corpus; train rank-8 LoRA and full FT to matched target IoU; measure zero-shot degradation; plot forgetting-per-gain vs task rank.
main_risk: Matching target IoU across methods may be impossible on the hardest tasks, complicating the exchange-rate comparison.
community_default_belief: LoRA is strictly gentler: less capacity means less damage; forgetting concerns favor PEFT unconditionally.
why_that_may_be_wrong: Capacity starvation doesn't cancel optimization pressure - it redirects it into whatever directions are available, which are shared with source capabilities precisely because rank is scarce.
fastest_falsification: One day: 2-convention vs 8-convention tasks, both methods; no trend in forgetting-per-gain falsifies.

consolidation.territory: T01 SAM / Foundation Model adaptation / PEFT

one_line: Calibration forgetting has a one-hour fix nobody applies: retraining only the IoU head post-adaptation restores self-assessment without touching masks.
problem: Adapted SAM checkpoints ship with IoU heads trained for the base model's error distribution (or blindly co-tuned); the head's repair is never treated as a separate cheap step.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Post-hoc IoU-head-only retraining (frozen everything else) on a few hundred target masks restores calibration to near-base levels for both target and source, because the head's inputs still contain sufficient quality-relevant signal - miscalibration is a readout mismatch, not information loss.
falsifiable_prediction: Head-only retraining will cut calibration error by more than half in most adapted checkpoints; the residual error will be predicted by how much the adapter changed the decoder features (measurable via CKA), identifying when the cheap fix fails.
why_important: If true, every deployed adapted SAM can gain reliable self-assessment for negligible cost - directly upgrading pseudo-label filtering and active learning; if false, feature changes destroy quality-signal itself, which is scientifically more alarming and worth knowing.
why_possibly_novel: [HYPOTHESIS] Isolating the IoU head as a post-hoc repairable module, with a feature-drift predictor of repair success, appears unexamined.
minimal_falsification_experiment: Take 3 adapted checkpoints; retrain IoU head on 300 labeled target instances; evaluate calibration on target + source probes; correlate residual miscalibration with decoder-feature CKA drift.
main_risk: 300 instances may under-sample the error distribution for domains with heavy-tailed difficulty.
community_default_belief: Calibration of adapted models is either ignored or assumed to require full recalibration pipelines / temperature scaling of a system that lacks logits.
why_that_may_be_wrong: The IoU head is a tiny MLP on decoder tokens - if quality signal survives adaptation (plausible since masks are decent), only the regression mapping needs updating.
fastest_falsification: Three hours: one checkpoint, head retrain, calibration before/after.

consolidation.territory: T01 SAM / Foundation Model adaptation / PEFT

one_line: SAM segments photometric contiguity, not objects: it has no amodal completion even when occlusion is trivially inferable, and this is quantifiable as a core defect.
problem: 'Segment anything' is interpreted as objecthood understanding; whether SAM's grouping is mere contiguous-appearance clustering has not been cleanly isolated.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] SAM's masks are governed by photometric contiguity: for objects split by thin occluders, SAM returns the visible fragment containing the click at rates near 100%, regardless of how visually obvious the completion is, and no prompt strategy recovers the full object reliably.
falsifiable_prediction: On synthetic scenes with parametric occluder width, the probability of whole-object masks will drop to near zero once fragments are photometrically separated, independent of completion difficulty for humans; multimask candidates will not contain the amodal option.
why_important: Downstream users assume object-level outputs (counting, tracking, robotics grasping); a contiguity-only grouper fails them in structured ways. Also defines a capability boundary that adaptation methods could target only if it is first measured.
why_possibly_novel: [HYPOTHESIS] Amodal failure is anecdotally known; a parametric, prompt-strategy-exhaustive quantification that separates 'cannot' from 'chooses not to' (checking all multimask candidates) appears missing.
minimal_falsification_experiment: Synthetic occlusion benchmark: objects with occluders of varying width/texture; click each fragment and the occluder; record whether ANY candidate mask at ANY prompt joins the fragments; compare with human completion judgments.
main_risk: Mostly confirmatory risk: the interesting outcome is the quantitative boundary (e.g., occluder width threshold), which may be uninterestingly sharp.
community_default_belief: SAM 'knows objects' - its masks are treated as object hypotheses in countless pipelines; occlusion handling is assumed partially present because training data contains occlusions.
why_that_may_be_wrong: SA-1B ground truth segments visible regions only ([KNOWN FACT] its masks are visible-region masks), so the training objective actively teaches against amodal grouping.
fastest_falsification: Three hours: 50 synthetic occlusions, exhaustive prompts; any reliable amodal completion falsifies.

consolidation.territory: T01 SAM / Foundation Model adaptation / PEFT

one_line: SAM hallucinates boundaries where contrast vanishes by snapping to the nearest strong edge - a predictable 'closed contour at any cost' prior.
problem: When part of an object's true boundary has zero local contrast, SAM still outputs a closed mask; where that invented boundary goes is unstudied though it determines error structure.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] In contrast-gap regions SAM does not interpolate smoothly (human-like completion) but snaps to the nearest strong irrelevant edge, with snap probability governed by edge strength and distance - making its hallucinations systematic and predictable by a simple local edge-field model.
falsifiable_prediction: On images with controlled contrast-gap arcs, predicted-boundary deviation will follow the nearest-strong-edge field rather than geodesic/smooth completion; a 2-parameter snap model (distance, strength) will explain most variance in where hallucinated boundaries land.
why_important: Predictable hallucination enables automatic flagging of untrustworthy boundary segments (high snap-risk zones) without ground truth - directly useful for QA in auto-labeling; also characterizes the model's implicit contour prior.
why_possibly_novel: [HYPOTHESIS] Modeling WHERE segmentation errors go (not just how large they are) as a falsifiable attractor model appears novel for SAM.
minimal_falsification_experiment: Generate objects with erased boundary arcs and controlled distractor edges at varying distance/strength; fit and cross-validate the snap model; test transfer of fitted parameters to real weak-boundary datasets.
main_risk: Real-image validation needs weak-boundary ground truth, which is scarce and noisy.
community_default_belief: Segmentation errors in low-contrast regions are treated as unstructured uncertainty - reported as lower boundary-F, not as systematic attraction to specific wrong answers.
why_that_may_be_wrong: The decoder must place a boundary somewhere; edge-following features are the strongest available signal, so deterministic snapping is the expected mechanism - yet no one has fit the deterministic model.
fastest_falsification: Four hours: synthetic contrast-gap set, overlay predictions on edge field; random deviation directions falsify.

consolidation.territory: T01 SAM / Foundation Model adaptation / PEFT

one_line: SAM's thin-structure failure is tokenization-limited, not knowledge-limited: failure onset sits at a fixed fraction of patch size and is cured by input upsampling, not by fine-tuning.
problem: Thin structures (wires, vessels, cracks) are a known weak spot, routinely attacked with fine-tuning or new architectures without establishing whether resolution alone is the binding constraint.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] There is a critical structure width, a fixed fraction of the 16px patch size, below which SAM fails regardless of domain familiarity - and above which it succeeds even zero-shot on unfamiliar domains; simple input upsampling shifts the failure point exactly as geometry predicts, while LoRA fine-tuning at native resolution does not shift it.
falsifiable_prediction: IoU-vs-width curves across 4 thin-structure domains will share a collapse point in patch-relative units; 2x upsampling will move it 2x; fine-tuning without resolution change will improve thick-structure IoU but leave the collapse point fixed.
why_important: Separates 'needs adaptation' from 'needs resolution' - a decision every deployment faces; predicts that much thin-structure fine-tuning effort is wasted on an information-theoretic wall.
why_possibly_novel: [HYPOTHESIS] The patch-relative invariance of the failure point and the FT-cannot-move-it claim appear untested as explicit predictions.
minimal_falsification_experiment: Synthetic + real thin structures with measured widths; evaluate zero-shot at {1x,2x,4x} input scales and after LoRA at 1x; locate collapse points in patch units.
main_risk: Tiling/memory constraints at 4x may introduce confounds (seams) requiring careful implementation.
community_default_belief: Thin-structure failure reflects missing domain knowledge or decoder capacity, hence fine-tune or redesign; resolution is a secondary engineering knob. [VERIFIED PRIOR WORK] Multiple works fine-tune SAM specifically for vessel/crack segmentation.
why_that_may_be_wrong: A one-patch-wide structure occupies a fraction of one token; no amount of weight adaptation can recover information destroyed by the tokenizer's low-pass behavior.
fastest_falsification: Four hours: one crack dataset, width-stratified IoU at 1x vs 2x; identical curves falsify (would indicate knowledge, not resolution).

consolidation.territory: T01 SAM / Foundation Model adaptation / PEFT

one_line: SAM learned an annotator, not nature: its output mask morphology (curvature spectra, corner statistics) matches SA-1B's machine-annotation style and differs measurably from human tracing.
problem: [KNOWN FACT] Most SA-1B masks were produced automatically by a model-in-the-loop pipeline. Whether SAM's outputs carry a detectable morphological fingerprint of that pipeline is unexamined.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] SAM outputs have a characteristic boundary-morphology signature (smoothness, curvature distribution, vertex/corner statistics) inherited from SA-1B's generation process, distinguishable from human-annotated morphology by a simple classifier even at matched accuracy.
falsifiable_prediction: A classifier on boundary-shape statistics will separate SAM masks from human masks of the SAME objects well above chance; the same statistics will place SA-1B masks closer to SAM outputs than to human-benchmark masks.
why_important: Establishes 'annotation-style inheritance' as a measurable contamination: datasets pseudo-labeled by SAM become morphologically homogeneous, biasing every model trained on them and enabling detection of SAM-generated labels in the wild (provenance auditing).
why_possibly_novel: [HYPOTHESIS] Morphological fingerprinting of foundation-model segmentation outputs, and its use for label-provenance detection, appears unproposed.
minimal_falsification_experiment: Collect datasets with careful human masks; run SAM with oracle prompts; extract boundary statistics; train/test style classifier with object-category controls; repeat on SA-1B samples.
main_risk: Style differences may be confounded with accuracy differences; must compare at matched IoU strata.
community_default_belief: A mask is a mask: quality is captured by IoU/boundary-F, and mask 'style' is not a recognized property with downstream consequences.
why_that_may_be_wrong: Generative pipelines imprint statistical regularities on outputs (as in image generation); segmentation masks are low-dimensional enough for the imprint to be both strong and measurable.
fastest_falsification: Six hours: 500 SAM-vs-human mask pairs, boundary-statistic classifier; chance-level separation falsifies.

consolidation.territory: T01 SAM / Foundation Model adaptation / PEFT

one_line: SAM has a contrast-polarity bias: at matched contrast magnitude, dark-object-on-light-ground and light-object-on-dark-ground are not segmented equally well.
problem: Low-level photometric biases of segmentation foundation models are uncharted; polarity is the simplest possible such bias and is directly consequential for modalities like X-ray and fluorescence where polarity is inverted relative to photographs.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] SAM performs systematically better on one contrast polarity (predicted: dark-on-light, reflecting photographic shadow/object statistics), with a gap that persists across shapes and scales and largely explains zero-shot deficits on polarity-inverted modalities.
falsifiable_prediction: On polarity-flipped synthetic and real image pairs (invert luminance, keep everything else), IoU will differ consistently in one direction; pre-inverting polarity-mismatched modalities (e.g., some microscopy) at inference will recover a large share of their zero-shot gap with zero training.
why_important: A zero-cost inference fix for entire modality families if confirmed; more broadly starts a catalog of low-level biases that adaptation studies should control before attributing gaps to 'domain semantics'.
why_possibly_novel: [HYPOTHESIS] Systematic polarity auditing of SAM, and polarity-inversion as an adaptation baseline, appear absent from the literature.
minimal_falsification_experiment: Luminance-inverted evaluation of standard benchmarks + synthetic controlled stimuli; then test inversion-preprocessing on 2 polarity-atypical modalities against LoRA baselines.
main_risk: Global inversion changes more than polarity perceptually (e.g., shadow semantics); synthetic controls are essential for clean attribution.
community_default_belief: SAM's zero-shot gaps on unusual modalities are attributed to high-level domain differences; low-level photometric conventions are not considered first-class explanations.
why_that_may_be_wrong: Natural photographs have strongly asymmetric luminance statistics ([KNOWN FACT] e.g., shadows are dark, skies are light), so polarity-dependent features are cheap for pretraining to acquire and hard to unlearn.
fastest_falsification: Two hours: invert 500 benchmark images, compare IoU; symmetric results falsify.

consolidation.territory: T01 SAM / Foundation Model adaptation / PEFT

one_line: SAM degrades much faster under high-frequency noise than under blur at matched distortion level, exposing edge-dependence over region-statistics grouping.
problem: Robustness of SAM is reported as aggregate corruption benchmarks; the informative comparison - which corruption family hurts more at matched severity - is not analyzed as evidence about grouping mechanisms.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] SAM's grouping relies dominantly on high-frequency edge evidence rather than region statistics: additive HF noise (which corrupts edges but preserves region means) will damage IoU far more than blur (which destroys HF but preserves large-scale region structure) at matched PSNR/SSIM.
falsifiable_prediction: The noise-vs-blur damage ratio at matched distortion will exceed a large factor; masks under blur will remain topologically correct while masks under noise will fragment; frequency-band ablation of inputs will locate the band SAM depends on.
