why_important: Mechanistic robustness profile predicts deployment failures (low-light sensor noise vs defocus) and prescribes the right augmentation for adaptation; frequency dependence also predicts which PEFT placements can help (early layers for band re-weighting).
why_possibly_novel: [HYPOTHESIS] Using matched-severity corruption asymmetry as an instrument to infer grouping mechanism (edges vs regions) in SAM appears unexploited.
minimal_falsification_experiment: Matched-PSNR ladder of Gaussian noise vs Gaussian blur on 3 datasets; IoU and topology metrics per rung; plus band-pass input ablations to map the critical frequency band.
main_risk: Matching 'severity' across corruption families is definitionally tricky; report multiple matching criteria (PSNR, SSIM, LPIPS) for robustness of conclusion.
community_default_belief: Robustness is a scalar property ('SAM is fairly robust to corruptions'); corruption families are averaged in benchmarks, implying no mechanism-revealing structure.
why_that_may_be_wrong: Averaging hides diagnostic asymmetries; a model built on edge-following should show a signature asymmetry that aggregate scores erase.
fastest_falsification: Three hours: one dataset, 3-rung ladder each family; symmetric degradation falsifies.

consolidation.territory: T01 SAM / Foundation Model adaptation / PEFT

one_line: SAM's transparency failure is inherited annotation convention, not perceptual limitation: it segments what SA-1B annotators outlined, and flips behavior when prompted at annotation-convention boundaries.
problem: SAM handles glass/water/reflection poorly; the standard reading is 'transparency is hard'. An alternative - that training labels were convention-inconsistent for transparent surfaces - is untested.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] For transparent objects, SA-1B labels mix conventions (sometimes the surface, sometimes the background seen through it); SAM internalized this mixture, so its transparency behavior is high-variance convention sampling rather than low-quality perception - and its multimask candidates often contain BOTH readings.
falsifiable_prediction: On transparent-object benchmarks, the correct surface mask will appear among SAM's 3 candidates far more often than top-1 accuracy suggests (large oracle gap specific to transparency); errors will cluster into the two convention modes rather than random shapes.
why_important: Re-attributes a famous failure from capability to label convention, changing the fix from architecture/data-scale to output selection or light-touch convention tuning; provides a template for auditing other 'hard categories' (mirrors, shadows, holes).
why_possibly_novel: [HYPOTHESIS] Convention-mixture as the explanatory model for transparency failure, with the oracle-gap signature as evidence, appears unexamined.
minimal_falsification_experiment: On a transparent-object dataset, measure top-1 vs best-of-3-candidates IoU gap for transparent vs opaque matched objects; cluster error masks; if oracle gap is transparency-specific and errors bimodal, hypothesis supported.
main_risk: Public transparency benchmarks are small; conclusions may need new annotations distinguishing surface vs see-through conventions.
community_default_belief: Transparent/specular materials are intrinsically hard for segmentation models due to weak visual evidence - a perception-capability framing. [VERIFIED PRIOR WORK] Dedicated glass/transparency segmentation literature exists on this premise.
why_that_may_be_wrong: SAM often produces confident, clean masks of the background-through-glass - not noisy failures - which is the signature of a learned alternative convention, not missing evidence.
fastest_falsification: Three hours: 100 transparent objects, oracle-gap and error-mode clustering.

consolidation.territory: T01 SAM / Foundation Model adaptation / PEFT

one_line: SAM binds attached shadows into object masks at a systematic, illumination-dependent rate - an unaudited labeling ambiguity every SAM-labeled dataset inherits.
problem: Whether cast/attached shadows belong to objects is convention-dependent; SAM's learned convention and its consistency are unknown, yet propagate into all auto-labeled data.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] SAM includes attached shadows at a stable rate that varies with shadow contrast and attachment geometry (predictable), rather than randomly - constituting a measurable convention with parameters, which downstream datasets absorb invisibly.
falsifiable_prediction: On shadow-annotated data, shadow-inclusion probability will be well fit by 2-3 stimulus parameters (contrast, contact length, penumbra width); the fitted convention will be stable across categories; SAM-pseudo-labeled datasets will show elevated shadow-inclusion vs human-labeled equivalents.
why_important: Quantifies a contamination channel for the growing ecosystem of SAM-labeled data (affects downstream photometric models, area estimates in agriculture/medicine); demonstrates how to audit foundation-model labeling conventions parametrically.
why_possibly_novel: [HYPOTHESIS] Parametric convention-auditing of SAM (fitting the convention's psychometric curve) appears novel; shadow handling is studied for removal, not for label-convention inheritance.
minimal_falsification_experiment: Use shadow-detection datasets with object masks; measure SAM shadow-inclusion vs stimulus parameters; fit psychometric curves; compare inclusion statistics of a public SAM-labeled corpus vs human-labeled corpus.
main_risk: Ground truth for 'attached shadow extent' is itself convention-laden; needs stimuli with unambiguous physical shadow masks (synthetic renders help).
community_default_belief: Shadow handling is noise in the labels - unsystematic error not worth modeling; dataset users assume SAM masks approximate human convention on average.
why_that_may_be_wrong: Training data conventions are learnable signal, not noise; a model that saw consistent shadow treatment will reproduce it consistently, making the 'average human convention' assumption quantitatively false.
fastest_falsification: Four hours: 200 shadowed objects, inclusion rate vs shadow contrast; a flat, near-zero or random relationship falsifies.

consolidation.territory: T01 SAM / Foundation Model adaptation / PEFT

one_line: SAM failure is predictable before prompting: a linear probe on encoder features forecasts achievable IoU, revealing a 'segmentability' direction in feature space.
problem: Failure prediction for SAM currently requires running prompts and reading the IoU head; whether failure is encoded pre-prompt in the image embedding is unknown.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] The encoder embedding contains a low-dimensional 'segmentability' signal: a linear readout on pooled/regional features predicts oracle-prompt achievable IoU with useful accuracy, before any prompting - implying failure is determined at encoding time, not decoding time.
falsifiable_prediction: A linear probe trained on one set of domains will predict achievable IoU on unseen domains with correlation >0.6; ablating the top probe directions from features will selectively degrade segmentation on hard-but-doable regions, evidencing causal relevance.
why_important: Pre-prompt triage enables routing (send to human / to bigger model / to adaptation) at encoder cost only; scientifically, locating failure at encode-time vs decode-time constrains where adaptation capacity should go.
why_possibly_novel: [HYPOTHESIS] Prompt-free failure forecasting for promptable segmentation, and the encode-vs-decode failure localization question, appear unstudied.
minimal_falsification_experiment: On 8 datasets: compute oracle-prompt IoU per region; train linear probes on frozen regional features from held-out domains; report cross-domain predictive correlation vs baselines (image quality metrics, entropy).
main_risk: The probe may learn dataset identity as a shortcut; cross-domain evaluation with domain-balanced regression targets is essential.
community_default_belief: Failure knowledge lives in the decoder/IoU head; the encoder is a neutral feature bank, and difficulty estimation requires prompting or a separate difficulty model.
why_that_may_be_wrong: Encoders trained for segmentation must represent boundary evidence quality; that representation is plausibly compact and linear - the community simply hasn't probed for it.
fastest_falsification: Six hours: 3 datasets, probe transfer test; near-zero transfer correlation falsifies.

consolidation.territory: T01 SAM / Foundation Model adaptation / PEFT

one_line: SAM is brittle on very large objects: masks degrade when objects exceed the relative-size range common in SA-1B, and simple crop-and-zoom-out inference fixes it.
problem: Scale generalization is assumed handled by the multi-scale nature of segmentation training; the upper tail (objects filling most of the frame) is rarely tested explicitly.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] SAM's quality drops systematically for objects above a relative-area threshold (a rarely-populated regime in web-photo mask statistics), with failure modes of under-segmentation into parts; padding the image to shrink relative object size restores quality - a pure dataset-prior failure.
falsifiable_prediction: IoU-vs-relative-area curves will show a decline above a threshold consistent across datasets; the same objects re-processed with 2x context padding will recover most loss; SA-1B's public mask-area statistics will show corresponding sparsity in that regime.
why_important: Close-up imagery (inspection, medical, document, macro) lives in this regime; a zero-training inference remedy would be broadly usable, and the result cleanly demonstrates dataset-prior leakage into a 'promptable' interface that should be scale-neutral.
why_possibly_novel: [HYPOTHESIS] Upper-tail scale brittleness with a causal fix (relative-size renormalization) appears undocumented; scale studies focus on small objects.
minimal_falsification_experiment: Stratify 5 benchmarks by object relative area; measure IoU curve; re-run large-object stratum with padding; correlate failure threshold with mask-area frequency in an SA-1B sample.
main_risk: Padding changes resolution-per-pixel too; must control by comparing against downsampled originals to separate scale-prior from resolution effects.
community_default_belief: Bigger objects are easier: more pixels, clearer evidence; segmentation difficulty is associated with small objects.
why_that_may_be_wrong: 'Easy' assumes in-distribution scale; a prompt on a frame-filling object resembles no training configuration, and the multimask prior defaults to part-level granularity.
fastest_falsification: Three hours: extreme close-up set, with/without padding; no recovery falsifies.

consolidation.territory: T01 SAM / Foundation Model adaptation / PEFT

one_line: The medical-SAM gap lives mostly downstream of the encoder: frozen encoder + retrained lightweight decoder recovers the bulk of full fine-tuning, because encoder features already separate anatomy.
problem: Medical adaptation methods modify the encoder by default ([VERIFIED PRIOR WORK] MedSAM-style full FT, SAMed-style encoder LoRA), without establishing whether encoder features are actually deficient for medical boundaries.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] SAM's frozen encoder features linearly separate most medical structure boundaries; the dominant gap is decoder/prompt-space mismatch (what to select, which granularity), so decoder-side retraining captures the majority of achievable gain on most medical 2D tasks.
falsifiable_prediction: Across >=6 medical datasets: (frozen-encoder + retrained decoder) will reach a high fraction (predicted >70%) of full-FT gain; pixelwise linear probes on frozen features will track achievable performance per dataset, identifying the minority of datasets where encoder truly limits.
why_important: Localizing the gap redirects the field's compute (decoder-side is 100x cheaper), enables shared-encoder multi-task deployment, and turns 'medical is out of distribution for SAM' from slogan into a decomposed, quantified claim.
why_possibly_novel: [HYPOTHESIS] A systematic encoder-sufficiency audit via probes + matched-budget decoder retraining across many medical sets appears missing; existing works assert encoder insufficiency implicitly.
minimal_falsification_experiment: 6 medical 2D datasets: linear pixel probes on frozen features; decoder-only retrain; encoder LoRA; full FT - all matched training budgets; decompose gains.
main_risk: 3D/volumetric tasks may behave differently; conclusion must be scoped to 2D slices initially.
community_default_belief: Medical images are far out of SAM's training distribution, so the encoder must be adapted; feature insufficiency is the assumed bottleneck.
why_that_may_be_wrong: Frozen-feature probes in other transfer settings routinely reveal features are better than task heads suggest; the medical gap may be largely about selection conventions (organs aren't 'objects' photometrically) which is decoder territory.
fastest_falsification: One day: 2 datasets, probe + decoder-retrain vs full FT; decoder-side capturing <30% of gain falsifies.

consolidation.territory: T01 SAM / Foundation Model adaptation / PEFT

one_line: Label conventions are portable modules: a decoder retrained on convention A over a frozen encoder transfers that convention to unseen domains without further training.
problem: Whether 'what to segment' generalizes independently of 'how to see' is untested; if conventions are decoder-portable, one convention module could serve many domains.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] A decoder retrained to implement a convention (e.g., 'always semantic-part granularity' or 'exclude holes') on dataset X will apply that convention zero-shot on unseen datasets Y, because conventions are readout policies over encoder-general features.
falsifiable_prediction: Convention-consistency metrics on unseen domains will jump toward the trained convention after decoder swap (without target-domain training), while plain accuracy on standard benchmarks is preserved; conventions requiring new perceptual distinctions will fail to transfer, mapping the boundary of readout-expressible conventions.
why_important: Would establish a factorization (perception vs convention) with practical value - convention libraries, instant re-conventioning of pipelines - and scientific value: identifying which segmentation semantics are 'linear readouts' over foundation features.
why_possibly_novel: [HYPOTHESIS] Convention transfer via decoder swap as an experimental paradigm appears novel; related decoder-retraining work targets accuracy, not convention portability.
minimal_falsification_experiment: Define 2 mechanical conventions applicable across datasets (hole treatment, part granularity); retrain decoders on one dataset each; evaluate convention-adherence on 3 unseen datasets vs base decoder.
main_risk: Defining convention-adherence metrics that don't require new annotation is the hard part; use mechanically-derivable relabelings.
community_default_belief: Adaptation is domain-bound: a decoder tuned on X is specialized to X's appearance and must be retuned elsewhere.
why_that_may_be_wrong: If encoder features are domain-general (as zero-shot SAM suggests), decoder policies over them should inherit that generality - the entanglement assumption is untested.
fastest_falsification: One day: hole-convention decoder, test on 2 unseen datasets; no convention transfer falsifies.

consolidation.territory: T01 SAM / Foundation Model adaptation / PEFT

one_line: Per-layer feature-shift profiles prescribe PEFT placement: the depth at which source-target CKA collapses predicts which layers need adapters, per domain.
problem: PEFT placement (which layers get adapters) is chosen by convention or global ablation, not by measuring where the specific domain's representations actually diverge.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] The layer-resolved divergence profile between target-domain features and natural-image features (CKA or subspace angle per layer, computable with unlabeled data) predicts the placement that maximizes adaptation efficiency: adapters placed at and after the divergence onset match full placement; earlier-only placement fails when divergence onsets late.
falsifiable_prediction: Across domains with early-onset vs late-onset divergence profiles, placement-restricted LoRA performance will follow the profile's prediction; a placement policy derived from 100 unlabeled images will match exhaustive placement search within noise.
why_important: Replaces placement search (expensive, per-domain) with a measurement; more deeply, tests whether representation-divergence localization is the right theory of where adaptation must act - a reusable principle beyond SAM.
why_possibly_novel: [HYPOTHESIS] Unlabeled divergence-profiling as a prescriptive placement policy with validated predictions appears new; CKA is used descriptively in transfer literature, not prescriptively for PEFT.
minimal_falsification_experiment: 8 domains: compute divergence profiles; classify onset depth; train LoRA with {early-only, late-only, onset-onward, all} placements at matched parameters; test profile-prediction agreement.
main_risk: Divergence measured on frozen features may misestimate where adaptation is needed if needed changes are in directions orthogonal to dominant variance (CKA blindspot).
community_default_belief: Apply LoRA to all attention layers - placement subtleties are second-order and not worth per-domain analysis.
why_that_may_be_wrong: Uniform placement wastes capacity where features already transfer and may under-allocate where they don't; the 'second-order' claim has never been tested against a measurement-driven policy.
fastest_falsification: One day: 2 contrasting domains (one sensor-shift, one convention-shift), profiles + 3 placements each.

consolidation.territory: T01 SAM / Foundation Model adaptation / PEFT

one_line: SAM's decoder allocates constant compute per object regardless of boundary complexity; its error scales with contour information content - a measurable compute-starvation law.
problem: [KNOWN FACT] SAM's mask decoder runs a fixed small number of attention operations per prompt, independent of object complexity; whether complex objects are compute-starved (vs feature-limited) is undetermined.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Boundary error per unit contour length grows with contour complexity (curvature entropy) under fixed decoder compute, and recursive self-prompting on error-dense sub-regions (giving the same decoder more passes) recovers accuracy - demonstrating starvation, not ignorance.
falsifiable_prediction: Error will correlate with contour complexity after controlling for size/contrast; iterative sub-region re-prompting will disproportionately help high-complexity objects, flattening the error-vs-complexity slope.
why_important: Identifies a scaling law tying output complexity to inference compute for promptable models - suggesting complexity-adaptive inference (not bigger models) is the correct fix, with direct cost/quality implications.
why_possibly_novel: [HYPOTHESIS] Formulating and testing a compute-vs-output-complexity starvation law for segmentation decoders appears new.
minimal_falsification_experiment: Stratify benchmarks by contour curvature entropy; measure per-stratum boundary error; implement sub-region re-prompting; compare slope flattening vs matched-extra-compute baselines (e.g., test-time augmentation).
main_risk: Complexity correlates with annotation noise in ground truth; need datasets with reliable complex boundaries (e.g., leaves, gears).
community_default_belief: Decoder capacity is 'enough' because average benchmarks look good; errors on complex objects are attributed to features or training data, and fixes proposed are architectural (heavier decoders).
why_that_may_be_wrong: Averages are dominated by simple contours; a fixed-compute readout mathematically cannot serialize unbounded boundary information - the question is only where the ceiling sits.
fastest_falsification: Six hours: complexity-stratified error analysis on 2 datasets; no complexity dependence after controls falsifies.

consolidation.territory: T01 SAM / Foundation Model adaptation / PEFT

one_line: Oracle decomposition of SAM's boundary error: feeding ground-truth low-res masks through the upsampling path measures exactly how much error is decoder-intrinsic vs upsampling-intrinsic.
problem: Boundary error in SAM conflates encoder resolution limits, decoder decisions, and the final upsampling stage; adaptation papers attack all three blindly because no error budget exists.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] A large, quantifiable share of fine-boundary error is introduced after the decoder's decision - in the low-res mask representation and fixed upsampling - such that oracle low-res masks passed through SAM's own output path already lose most of the boundary-F headroom that fine-tuning papers chase.
falsifiable_prediction: The oracle pipeline (GT mask downsampled to decoder resolution, then SAM's upsampling) will exhibit a boundary-F ceiling substantially below 1.0, and the gap between SAM's actual boundary-F and this ceiling will be small on many domains - implying most 'boundary improvements' from PEFT are impossible unless the representation resolution changes.
why_important: An error budget stops misattributed effort: if the ceiling explains most boundary loss, encoder/decoder fine-tuning for boundaries is provably near-futile, and honest comparisons of boundary-improvement methods must report headroom.
why_possibly_novel: [HYPOTHESIS] Publishing an oracle-based error budget for SAM's output path, and auditing adaptation papers' claims against representational ceilings, appears not to have been done.
minimal_falsification_experiment: On 5 datasets: compute oracle-path boundary-F ceiling per dataset; place SAM's zero-shot and LoRA-adapted boundary-F against it; report headroom-normalized gains of adaptation.
main_risk: Details of mask thresholding/interpolation in the oracle path must exactly mirror SAM's; implementation errors would corrupt the budget.
community_default_belief: Boundary quality is a learnable property: fine-tuning with boundary losses or better data improves it; representational ceilings are not part of the discourse.
why_that_may_be_wrong: [KNOWN FACT] SAM predicts masks at low internal resolution with fixed upsampling; information-theoretic limits at that resolution are unavoidable regardless of training, and may already bind on real data.
fastest_falsification: Three hours: one dataset's oracle ceiling; if ceiling is ~1.0 (upsampling is lossless in practice), the budget hypothesis collapses.

consolidation.territory: T01 SAM / Foundation Model adaptation / PEFT

one_line: SAM's IoU head is a domain-difficulty meter, not an instance-quality meter: it ranks datasets well but barely ranks instances within an image.
problem: The IoU head's outputs are consumed as per-instance quality estimates; the decomposition of its predictive power (between-domain vs within-domain vs within-image) has never been reported.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Most of the IoU head's correlation with true quality comes from coarse difficulty factors (domain, image quality, object size) - within-image, across candidate masks of comparable size, its instance-level resolution is near chance, making it unfit for its primary use case (picking the best mask).
falsifiable_prediction: Variance decomposition will show between-dataset correlation >> within-image correlation; substituting the IoU head with a simple covariate model (size, contrast, domain id) will match its filtering performance in auto-labeling pipelines.
why_important: The entire mask-filtering ecosystem trusts these scores; showing they are difficulty covariates in disguise would force re-design of selection (e.g., jitter-variance from idea W15-B001-A-009) and re-interpretation of published pipelines' claimed precision.
why_possibly_novel: [HYPOTHESIS] A variance-decomposition audit of SAM's self-assessment across granularity levels appears unpublished.
minimal_falsification_experiment: On 6 datasets: collect (predicted IoU, true IoU) pairs; decompose correlation between-dataset / between-image / within-image; build the covariate baseline; compare pipeline-level filtering outcomes.
main_risk: Within-image comparisons need multiple comparable candidates per prompt; restricted to multimask outputs, which limits sample diversity.
community_default_belief: Predicted IoU is a per-mask quality estimate - that is its designed function and how every pipeline uses it.
why_that_may_be_wrong: Regression heads trained under distribution-matched conditions learn the easiest predictive covariates; instance-specific quality signal is much harder to extract than difficulty covariates, so the head plausibly never learned it.
fastest_falsification: Four hours: within-image rank correlation on 2 datasets; strong within-image resolution falsifies.

consolidation.territory: T01 SAM / Foundation Model adaptation / PEFT

one_line: Few-shot SAM adaptation follows a power law with a domain-invariant exponent: only the offset moves across domains, so 10 labeled images predict the value of 1000.
problem: Annotation budgeting for adaptation is guesswork; no functional form of the few-shot curve is established for promptable segmentation.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Target IoU vs number of labeled images under fixed LoRA follows a shifted power law whose exponent is (approximately) shared across domains for a fixed model/method; domains differ mainly in offset (zero-shot level) and asymptote.
falsifiable_prediction: Fitting the law on n<=10 images will predict n=500 performance within a small margin across >=8 domains; exponent estimates across domains will cluster tightly compared to offsets; violations will concentrate in domains with label-convention conflicts (diagnosable separately).
why_important: A predictive law converts 'should we annotate more?' into arithmetic - the single most common practical question in adaptation - and constrains theory (shared exponent implies shared learning mechanism across domains).
why_possibly_novel: [VERIFIED PRIOR WORK] Scaling laws exist for pretraining; [HYPOTHESIS] a validated few-shot adaptation law with cross-domain exponent invariance for segmentation PEFT appears unestablished.
minimal_falsification_experiment: 8 domains x n in {2,5,10,30,100,300} x 3 seeds with fixed LoRA recipe; fit per-domain power laws; test exponent clustering and small-n extrapolation error.
main_risk: Few-shot regime is seed-noisy; requires enough seeds for stable fits, and the law may break at n<5.
community_default_belief: Few-shot adaptation curves are domain-idiosyncratic; extrapolation from 10 images is considered unreliable folklore rather than modelable.
why_that_may_be_wrong: Fixed model + fixed update family screens off most domain idiosyncrasy; remaining variation may be low-dimensional exactly as in pretraining scaling laws.
fastest_falsification: One day: 3 domains, 4 budget points; wildly different exponents falsify.

consolidation.territory: T01 SAM / Foundation Model adaptation / PEFT
consolidation.solo_drop_note: Weakest member of HC-11: descriptive scaling-curve fitting with a soft 'approximately shared exponent' claim; dominated by actionable siblings (A-052 selection, A-057 hardness curriculum) that would generate the same curves as a byproduct.

one_line: Which images you label beats how many: feature-space coverage selection (k-center on frozen SAM features) matches 3x random labels for LoRA adaptation.
problem: Adaptation datasets are typically labeled by convenience sampling; the exchange rate between selection quality and quantity is unmeasured for SAM PEFT.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Because LoRA needs to observe the domain's feature-shift directions (not its full appearance diversity), a small set chosen to cover frozen-feature space supports adaptation as well as much larger random sets; marginal value of a labeled image is predicted by its feature-space distance to already-selected images.
falsifiable_prediction: k-center-selected n images will match random 2-3n across domains; the benefit will shrink for domains with intrinsically low-dimensional shift (any images suffice) as predicted by shift-spectrum measurements (link to W15-B001-A-021).
why_important: Direct annotation-cost reduction with a zero-training selection procedure; ties active selection theory to the geometry of what PEFT actually learns.
why_possibly_novel: [VERIFIED PRIOR WORK] Core-set selection exists for classification active learning; [HYPOTHESIS] its exchange-rate quantification for foundation-segmentation PEFT, with shift-dimension moderation, appears new.
minimal_falsification_experiment: 5 domains: label budgets {10,30} selected by k-center vs random vs cluster-stratified; train identical LoRA; measure exchange rate; correlate benefit with measured shift dimensionality.
main_risk: k-center may over-select outliers/noise images in dirty pools; robustified variants may be needed, complicating the clean claim.
community_default_belief: More labels are better and selection refinements yield marginal gains; annotation effort discussions center on count, not composition.
why_that_may_be_wrong: For low-rank adaptation the training signal saturates once shift directions are covered - after that, additional random images are nearly redundant by construction.
fastest_falsification: Six hours: one domain, k-center-10 vs random-30.

consolidation.territory: T01 SAM / Foundation Model adaptation / PEFT
consolidation.mutation_note: MUTATE. k-center/coreset selection applied to SAM-LoRA is a known-method permutation. Salvage: recast as the claim that a labeled image's adaptation value is predicted by its coverage of the domain's feature-shift directions (measurable pre-training from frozen-feature discrepancy spectra; ties to A-021). Kill the 'selection beats random' framing.

one_line: LoRA rank is a label-noise filter: low rank cannot fit incoherent boundary noise, creating a measurable rank-noise crossover that inverts method rankings on dirty data.
problem: Label noise (loose boundaries, inconsistent conventions) is pervasive in adaptation data, but PEFT capacity and noise robustness are studied separately.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Incoherent per-image boundary noise requires high-rank updates to memorize; low-rank LoRA is therefore implicitly robust, and there exists a predictable noise-level crossover where rank-4 outperforms rank-64 on clean-test IoU despite losing on train fit.
falsifiable_prediction: Injecting parametric boundary noise (random dilation/erosion per instance) will produce the crossover; the crossover noise level will shift with dataset size as memorization theory predicts; consistent (systematic) label bias will NOT produce the crossover - only incoherent noise will.
why_important: Gives practitioners a principled rank rule based on estimated label quality; separates two confused notions (capacity for task vs capacity for noise); explains contradictory rank recommendations across papers whose datasets differ in cleanliness.
why_possibly_novel: [HYPOTHESIS] Rank-as-noise-filter with a quantified crossover and the coherent-vs-incoherent noise distinction appears untested for segmentation PEFT.
minimal_falsification_experiment: One clean dataset; noise levels {0,2,5,10}px incoherent + one systematic-bias arm; ranks {4,16,64}; 3 seeds; map test-IoU surfaces and locate crossovers.
main_risk: Synthetic noise may not represent real annotator noise structure; validate on a naturally noisy dataset with a cleaned test subset.
community_default_belief: Label noise hurts all methods similarly, and rank choice is about task complexity and dataset size, not label quality.
why_that_may_be_wrong: Memorizing N independent boundary perturbations requires update dimensionality growing with N - exactly what rank caps; the interaction is mathematically forced yet absent from practice guides.
fastest_falsification: Six hours: 5px noise, rank 4 vs 64; no ranking inversion at any noise level falsifies.

consolidation.territory: T01 SAM / Foundation Model adaptation / PEFT

one_line: Prompt diversity in fine-tuning beats image diversity: varying prompts on few images adapts SAM better than center-clicks on many images at equal annotation cost.
problem: Adaptation recipes fix a prompt-generation policy (often GT-box or center point) and scale images; the prompt-axis of training-data diversity is unexamined as a budget dimension.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] SAM adaptation is substantially prompt-conditional behavior learning; covering the prompt distribution (positions, types, counts) on FEW images transfers better than covering image variation with a degenerate prompt policy - because the decoder's prompt-response map, not the encoder's appearance map, is what most domains need rewritten.
falsifiable_prediction: At matched mask-label cost, (5 images x 20 prompt configurations) will beat (100 images x 1 center prompt) on prompt-robust evaluation across several domains; the advantage will disappear when evaluation uses only the training prompt policy - exposing that standard evaluations hide prompt overfitting.
why_important: Reorders the annotation recipe (prompt sampling is free once a mask exists); reveals 'prompt overfitting' as a hidden failure of current adapted models under user-style prompting variability.
why_possibly_novel: [HYPOTHESIS] Treating prompt-space coverage as a training-data axis with a measurable exchange rate against image count appears novel.
minimal_falsification_experiment: 3 domains; fixed mask budget; arms: image-rich/prompt-poor, image-poor/prompt-rich, balanced; evaluate under diverse simulated prompt policies including out-of-policy prompts.
main_risk: Prompt configurations are cheap but correlated; effective diversity may saturate quickly making the rich arm equivalent to balanced.
community_default_belief: Adaptation quality is bottlenecked by image/label count; prompts are generated by a fixed script and considered an implementation detail not worth reporting.
why_that_may_be_wrong: The interface being adapted IS the prompt-response function; leaving its input distribution degenerate while varying images optimizes the wrong marginal.
fastest_falsification: Six hours: one domain, the two extreme arms, prompt-robust evaluation.

consolidation.territory: T01 SAM / Foundation Model adaptation / PEFT

one_line: SAM self-training plateaus by design: its confidence errors are correlated with the domain gap, so pseudo-label selection recruits exactly the wrong examples - confident-and-wrong is systematic, not random.
problem: Self-training adapted SAMs on their own filtered outputs is a popular label-free recipe; why it saturates quickly (when it does) lacks a mechanistic account.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Under domain shift, the IoU head's errors are anti-correlated with true difficulty of the shift-specific failure modes: the model is most confidently wrong precisely on the patterns that define the domain gap, so confidence-filtered self-training reinforces base-model biases and cannot learn the gap.
falsifiable_prediction: Stratifying pseudo-labels by (confidence, correctness): the confident-wrong stratum will be enriched in gap-defining patterns (identified via error clustering); self-training gains will track the fraction of gap patterns that survive filtering; replacing confidence filtering with jitter-agreement filtering (W15-B001-A-009) will raise the plateau measurably.
why_important: Explains a widely observed plateau with a testable mechanism and provides a fix; more generally warns that self-assessment learned in-domain is structurally unable to supervise out-of-domain learning - a foundational limit for autonomous adaptation.
why_possibly_novel: [HYPOTHESIS] The 'confidence errors aligned with gap' mechanism, and its stratified test for promptable segmentation, appear unformalized.
minimal_falsification_experiment: 2 shifted domains: run one self-training round; stratify pseudo-labels; cluster confident-wrong instances; compare plateaus under confidence vs jitter-agreement filtering at matched kept-fraction.
main_risk: Error clustering interpretation is subjective; needs quantitative gap-pattern definitions (e.g., via labeled diagnostic subsets).
community_default_belief: Self-training fails from generic confirmation bias/noise accumulation; better thresholds or teacher-student tricks are the assumed remedies.
why_that_may_be_wrong: Generic noise would be filterable by better thresholds; if wrongness is structured and confidence-aligned, thresholds cannot help - a qualitatively different and fixable failure.
fastest_falsification: One day: stratification + one self-training round on one domain; finding confident-wrong to be pattern-random falsifies.

consolidation.territory: T01 SAM / Foundation Model adaptation / PEFT

one_line: One human-corrected box per image is enough: adaptation on SAM-generated masks accepted/fixed via box prompts matches dense manual annotation at a fraction of cost.
problem: The assumed gold standard for adaptation data is dense manual masks; the minimal human signal sufficient for equal adaptation quality is unquantified.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] For most domains, the information adaptation needs is low-bandwidth (conventions + shift directions); a workflow of [SAM proposes with box prompt -> human accepts or adjusts box -> mask kept if IoU-proxy passes] yields training data whose adaptation value equals dense annotation, because residual mask errors are incoherent (see W15-B001-A-053) and get filtered by low rank.
falsifiable_prediction: LoRA trained on box-workflow labels will match dense-label LoRA within noise on >=4 of 6 domains; failures will concentrate where SAM's proposal errors are systematic (measurable via error-coherence statistics), giving a predictive applicability test.
why_important: Order-of-magnitude annotation savings with a falsifiable applicability criterion; also empirically measures the 'information content' human supervision must add over foundation-model priors - a quantity of scientific interest.
why_possibly_novel: [HYPOTHESIS] Equal-quality (not just cheaper-but-worse) weak-workflow adaptation with a coherence-based failure predictor appears unestablished; existing weak-label work reports degradation without the predictive criterion.
minimal_falsification_experiment: 6 domains: simulate the box workflow from GT (box from GT, accept SAM mask); train LoRA on workflow vs dense labels; compare; compute SAM-error coherence per domain and test as failure predictor.
main_risk: Simulated acceptance may be optimistic vs real human behavior; a small real-annotator study would be needed for the strong claim.
community_default_belief: Weak/cheap labels trade quality for cost; dense expert masks remain necessary for high-quality domain adaptation, especially medical.
why_that_may_be_wrong: When the pretrained model already produces near-correct masks, dense annotation mostly re-encodes what the model knows; the human's unique contribution is a few bits (which object, roughly where), which boxes convey.
fastest_falsification: Six hours: one domain, workflow-vs-dense LoRA.

consolidation.territory: T01 SAM / Foundation Model adaptation / PEFT
consolidation.mutation_note: MUTATE. SAM-proposes/human-verifies is standard annotation-tooling practice (workflow permutation). Salvage: isolate the falsifiable core - residual SAM mask errors are per-domain incoherent and hence un-memorizable by low-rank updates - and make measured error-coherence the predictor of when cheap verification matches dense labels (complements A-053).

one_line: Anti-curriculum wins for PEFT: training on SAM's WORST zero-shot images first accelerates adaptation, because easy images provide near-zero gradient through a strong prior.
problem: Example-ordering effects for adapting strong priors are unstudied; curriculum intuitions from scratch-training may invert when the model already performs well on 'easy' examples.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] For LoRA on SAM, images where zero-shot already succeeds contribute negligible learning signal; front-loading high-error images (anti-curriculum by zero-shot IoU) reaches target performance in fewer steps and, in the few-shot regime, selecting ONLY hard images beats matched random selection - inverting classic curriculum advice.
falsifiable_prediction: Steps-to-target-IoU: hard-first < random < easy-first, with the gap growing as zero-shot performance rises; in fixed 20-image budgets, hardest-20 will beat random-20 unless hard images are label-noisy (measurable moderator).
why_important: Ordering and selection are free levers; more fundamentally, quantifies the 'gradient shadow' cast by a strong prior - a phenomenon that should reshape curriculum thinking for all foundation-model adaptation.
why_possibly_novel: [HYPOTHESIS] Prior-strength-dependent inversion of curriculum benefit, tested on segmentation PEFT, appears unreported.
minimal_falsification_experiment: 3 domains: order arms {easy-first, hard-first, random} for full sets; selection arms {hardest-k, random-k} for k=20; 3 seeds; track steps-to-target and final IoU.
main_risk: Hardness by zero-shot IoU conflates label noise with difficulty; needs a noise-audited subset.
community_default_belief: Curriculum (easy-to-hard) helps or at worst is neutral; hard-example mining is for late-stage training, not initialization of adaptation.
why_that_may_be_wrong: Curriculum theory assumes the model must build representations progressively; an adapted foundation model already has them - remaining learning is gap-specific, and the gap lives in the hard examples by definition.
fastest_falsification: Six hours: one domain, hardest-20 vs random-20.

consolidation.territory: T01 SAM / Foundation Model adaptation / PEFT

one_line: Few-shot medical SAM results are inflated by identity leakage: per-patient splits reveal that a chunk of reported adaptation gain is patient-specific memorization, not domain learning.
problem: Small medical adaptation sets often contain multiple slices/images per patient; many published splits are image-level. The size of the resulting optimism bias for PEFT specifically is unmeasured.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] LoRA has enough capacity to memorize patient-level appearance; image-level splits therefore overstate generalization, and the inflation grows with rank and shrinks with patient count - making some published few-shot rankings between PEFT methods artifacts of differential memorization.
falsifiable_prediction: On datasets with patient metadata, (image-split IoU - patient-split IoU) will be substantial in few-shot regimes, increase with LoRA rank, and correlate inversely with patients-per-training-set; re-evaluating public method comparisons under patient splits will change at least some orderings.
why_important: Evaluation integrity for a rapidly growing literature; provides the quantitative correction factor and a protocol (patient-split + rank-sensitivity report) that reviewers can demand.
why_possibly_novel: [VERIFIED PRIOR WORK] Identity leakage is a known concern in medical ML generally; [HYPOTHESIS] its interaction with PEFT capacity (rank-dependence) and its effect on SAM-adaptation method rankings appear unquantified.
minimal_falsification_experiment: 2 datasets with patient IDs: matched image-level vs patient-level splits x ranks {4,64} x 3 seeds; measure the leakage gap and rank interaction; re-run 2 published baselines under both protocols.
main_risk: Public datasets with clean patient metadata and enough patients are limited; may constrain domain diversity of the claim.
community_default_belief: Random image splits are acceptable for adaptation studies; PEFT's small parameter count is assumed to preclude meaningful memorization.
why_that_may_be_wrong: Rank-64 LoRA on a ViT-H-scale encoder is millions of parameters ([KNOWN FACT] order-of-magnitude arithmetic) - ample for encoding a handful of patients' appearance signatures.
fastest_falsification: Six hours: one dataset, both splits at rank 64.

consolidation.territory: T01 SAM / Foundation Model adaptation / PEFT

one_line: Augmentation and rank are exchangeable currencies: target-style augmentation lets rank-r match rank-4r, implying PEFT capacity partially substitutes for data diversity.
problem: Augmentation policies and LoRA capacity are tuned independently; whether they trade off along a measurable frontier is unknown.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Style-space augmentation (histogram/stain/noise transforms sampled around the target distribution) reduces the rank needed for a given accuracy by a quantifiable factor, because augmentation removes nuisance directions from the required update, shrinking its intrinsic rank (link to W15-B001-A-012).
falsifiable_prediction: Iso-accuracy contours in the (rank, augmentation-strength) plane will show smooth substitution; measured update stable-rank will DECREASE with augmentation strength at fixed accuracy - direct mechanistic evidence; over-augmentation will show as contour reversal.
why_important: Provides a principled way to hit accuracy targets under parameter budgets (edge deployment) and connects data-side and parameter-side adaptation theory through a measurable quantity (update rank).
why_possibly_novel: [HYPOTHESIS] The substitution frontier and the update-rank mediation mechanism appear untested; augmentation is usually evaluated as accuracy-additive, not capacity-sparing.
minimal_falsification_experiment: 2 domains: grid over ranks {2,4,8,16,32} x augmentation strengths {none, mild, strong}; map iso-accuracy contours; measure converged update stable-ranks.
main_risk: Defining comparable 'augmentation strength' across transform families is messy; use a distributional distance to target as the axis.
community_default_belief: Augmentation adds robustness; rank adds capacity - separate knobs addressing separate problems, tuned independently.
why_that_may_be_wrong: Both act on the same object (the update the optimizer must find); anything that simplifies the required update spends less capacity - the accounting has just never been done.
fastest_falsification: Six hours: one domain, rank-4+strong-aug vs rank-16+none.

consolidation.territory: T01 SAM / Foundation Model adaptation / PEFT

one_line: SAM's multimask disagreement is a better active-learning acquisition signal than its confidence: annotate where the model sees multiple plausible answers, not where it claims low quality.
problem: Active learning for SAM adaptation defaults to low-predicted-IoU acquisition; SAM's unique multimask output offers an unexploited disagreement signal whose acquisition value is untested.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Instances with high multimask disagreement carry more adaptation-relevant information per label (they localize convention/granularity uncertainty, which is what adaptation must resolve) than low-confidence instances (which mix noise, difficulty, and out-of-scope junk); disagreement-based acquisition yields faster IoU gains per label.
falsifiable_prediction: Label-efficiency curves: disagreement-acquired labels will dominate confidence-acquired and random on convention-shifted domains, but NOT on pure appearance-shift domains (where disagreement is low everywhere) - a double dissociation matching the mechanism.
why_important: Improves the label economics of every SAM adaptation loop with a zero-cost signal; the predicted dissociation also gives a field-usable diagnostic of gap type (links W15-B001-A-008).
why_possibly_novel: [HYPOTHESIS] Using intra-model output multiplicity (rather than ensembles or confidence) for acquisition in segmentation adaptation appears unstudied.
minimal_falsification_experiment: 4 domains (2 convention-shift, 2 appearance-shift): AL loops of 5 rounds x 10 labels with {disagreement, confidence, random, jitter-variance} acquisition; compare curves.
main_risk: Multimask disagreement may saturate (all-agree) after the first adaptation round, requiring signal refresh strategies.
community_default_belief: Uncertainty (low confidence) marks the most valuable labels; SAM's multimask output is a UX feature for pick-the-best, not an epistemic signal.
why_that_may_be_wrong: Confidence confounds several causes of error, most of which labels can't fix; disagreement specifically flags resolvable ambiguity - the label's comparative advantage.
fastest_falsification: One day: one convention-shift domain, disagreement vs confidence acquisition, 3 rounds.

consolidation.territory: T01 SAM / Foundation Model adaptation / PEFT
consolidation.mutation_note: MUTATE. Multimask-spread acquisition is query-by-committee with SAM as the committee (known-AL permutation). Salvage: drop the AL race; test the informational claim that multimask disagreement specifically localizes convention/granularity uncertainty while low confidence mixes noise, difficulty and junk. Fold the measurement into the A-061/A-089 family.

one_line: SAM as a disagreement oracle: the spread among its multimask outputs predicts where human annotators will disagree with each other.
problem: Inter-annotator disagreement is expensive to measure (multiple annotations per item) yet crucial for dataset design; no model-based predictor of human disagreement exists for segmentation.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] SAM's multimask spread was trained on exactly the ambiguity structure that drives human disagreement (one click, many valid masks), so its spread metrics predict inter-annotator IoU variance on the same instances - making SAM a cheap simulator of annotation ambiguity.
falsifiable_prediction: On datasets with multiple human annotations per instance, SAM spread will correlate with inter-annotator variance substantially above image-statistic baselines (edge density, size); the correlation will hold zero-shot across domains including medical (where multi-annotator data exists).
why_important: Enables ambiguity-aware dataset design (route ambiguous items to multiple annotators), fair model evaluation (down-weight ambiguous instances), and annotation-cost prediction - all from a free forward pass.
why_possibly_novel: [HYPOTHESIS] Validating a foundation model's output multiplicity against human disagreement statistics appears undone for segmentation.
minimal_falsification_experiment: Use multi-annotator segmentation datasets (medical multi-rater sets exist [VERIFIED PRIOR WORK] as a category); compute SAM spread vs inter-rater variance; compare against baselines; test cross-domain transfer of the relationship.
main_risk: Multi-rater datasets are concentrated in medical imaging - domain coverage of the validation will be narrow initially.
community_default_belief: Human disagreement reflects expertise and guideline differences that a label-free model cannot capture; ambiguity measurement requires actual multiple annotations.
why_that_may_be_wrong: A large share of disagreement is stimulus-driven (weak boundaries, granularity choices) - precisely the signal SAM's multimask machinery was optimized to represent.
fastest_falsification: Four hours: one multi-rater dataset, spread-vs-variance correlation; baseline-level correlation falsifies.

consolidation.territory: T01 SAM / Foundation Model adaptation / PEFT

one_line: The IoU head's overconfidence is a calibrated domain-distance meter: mean (predicted minus actual) IoU rises monotonically with domain shift, giving a labeled-data-free gap measurement.
problem: Estimating 'how far' a target domain is from SAM's competence currently requires labeled evaluation; a label-free gap meter would guide adaptation decisions but none is validated.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] The IoU head fails in a systematically optimistic direction under shift, and the magnitude of optimism (estimable with few labels, or label-free via jitter-agreement as ground-truth proxy) is a monotone, roughly domain-rankable function of true zero-shot performance drop.
falsifiable_prediction: Across 10+ domains, mean overconfidence will rank domains by true zero-shot gap with high rank-correlation; the label-free variant (predicted IoU minus jitter-agreement proxy) will preserve most of that correlation.
why_important: A practical instrument: decide between {use zero-shot, adapt, collect data} from unlabeled target images alone; scientifically, characterizes the failure geometry of learned self-assessment under shift (optimism, not noise).
why_possibly_novel: [HYPOTHESIS] Using self-assessment bias as a domain-gap measurement instrument, with label-free proxying, appears unproposed for segmentation.
minimal_falsification_experiment: 12 datasets spanning shift levels: compute true gap (labeled), mean overconfidence (labeled), and label-free proxy; report rank correlations and failure cases.
main_risk: Non-monotone regimes possible (extreme shift may produce chaotic rather than optimistic predictions), breaking the meter exactly where it's most needed.
community_default_belief: Confidence under shift is 'unreliable' - a reason to ignore it, not an instrument; domain gap estimation is done via labeled probes or feature distances.
why_that_may_be_wrong: Unreliable-with-structure is measurable signal: optimism arises mechanistically (head trained where masks were good), so its magnitude should track how wrong that assumption is - i.e., the gap itself.
fastest_falsification: Four hours: 5 domains, overconfidence vs true-gap rank correlation.

consolidation.territory: T01 SAM / Foundation Model adaptation / PEFT

one_line: Adapt the self-knowledge, not the skill: retraining only SAM's uncertainty pathway captures most of the active-learning and filtering value of full domain adaptation.
problem: Adaptation always targets mask quality; but many pipelines consume SAM's outputs THROUGH a filtering/routing layer, where what matters is knowing-when-wrong, not being-right more often.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] For pipeline-level outcomes (auto-label precision at fixed recall, human-routing efficiency), recalibrating the uncertainty pathway on the target domain (IoU head + a small feature adapter feeding it) achieves a large fraction of the value of full LoRA adaptation at a tiny fraction of the risk (zero mask-behavior change, zero forgetting).
falsifiable_prediction: On auto-labeling pipelines across 4 domains, uncertainty-only adaptation will recover >50% of full adaptation's pipeline-metric gain; combining unadapted masks + adapted uncertainty will beat adapted masks + stale uncertainty in at least some domains - a provocative inversion.
why_important: Reframes adaptation targets around system value rather than model accuracy; offers a zero-forgetting adaptation mode deployable where mask-behavior change is regulated (medical devices).
why_possibly_novel: [HYPOTHESIS] Uncertainty-pathway-only adaptation as a deliberate alternative (not a component) to skill adaptation appears unexplored.
minimal_falsification_experiment: 4 domains: arms {none, uncertainty-only, LoRA-full, both}; evaluate pipeline metrics (precision@recall of kept masks, human-review load at fixed error); compare value fractions.
main_risk: Where base masks are catastrophically bad, no amount of self-knowledge recovers pipeline value - applicability boundary must be mapped (ties to gap-meter W15-B001-A-062).
community_default_belief: Adaptation means improving masks; calibration is a post-processing nicety, and nobody would ship an unadapted model with adapted confidence.
why_that_may_be_wrong: In selective-prediction theory, system utility depends on both skill and self-knowledge; when skill is adequate-but-unreliable, the self-knowledge term dominates the utility gradient - a regime plausibly common for SAM.
fastest_falsification: Six hours: one domain, uncertainty-only vs full, pipeline precision@recall.

consolidation.territory: T01 SAM / Foundation Model adaptation / PEFT

one_line: Ambiguity is conserved under adaptation: images ambiguous for zero-shot SAM remain ambiguous after LoRA fine-tuning - the ambiguity lives in the data, not the weights.
problem: Whether fine-tuning resolves, redistributes, or preserves instance-level ambiguity is unknown; the answer determines whether ambiguity measurements transfer across model versions.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Per-instance ambiguity rankings (multimask spread, jitter variance) are highly rank-correlated before vs after adaptation, even as absolute accuracy improves - because ambiguity reflects stimulus properties (weak evidence, valid alternatives) that no in-distribution training removes.
falsifiable_prediction: Spearman correlation of instance ambiguity pre/post adaptation will exceed 0.8 across domains; exceptions will be convention ambiguities (resolvable by labels) vs evidence ambiguities (not) - and separating the two via which ambiguities collapse under training becomes a measurable decomposition.
why_important: If conserved, ambiguity maps computed once transfer across all future adapted versions (big practical savings), and the collapse-vs-persist split gives an operational definition of aleatoric vs resolvable uncertainty for segmentation - a conceptual contribution.
why_possibly_novel: [HYPOTHESIS] Testing ambiguity conservation across fine-tuning, and using training itself as the instrument to split ambiguity types, appears novel.
minimal_falsification_experiment: 3 domains: measure instance ambiguity pre/post LoRA (same probe prompts); compute rank correlations; cluster collapsed vs persistent ambiguities and inspect against convention-vs-evidence codings.
main_risk: Diversity collapse from fine-tuning (W15-B001-A-023) may suppress the ambiguity SIGNAL while ambiguity persists - need jitter-based measures robust to multimask collapse.
community_default_belief: Fine-tuning on a domain resolves the model's confusion there; ambiguity is treated as a model deficiency that training fixes.
why_that_may_be_wrong: Ambiguity is substantially a property of stimuli and label conventions; training changes the model's decision but cannot add evidence the pixels lack - conservation is the physically expected outcome.
fastest_falsification: Four hours: one domain pre/post checkpoint pair, ambiguity rank correlation.

consolidation.territory: T01 SAM / Foundation Model adaptation / PEFT

one_line: Two knobs, two uncertainties: multimask spread measures data ambiguity while prompt-jitter variance measures model uncertainty - and they decouple exactly on out-of-domain inputs.
problem: SAM offers two cheap output-multiplicity signals; whether they measure the same thing or complementary things (the aleatoric/epistemic split) is uncharacterized.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Multimask spread (same input, alternative interpretations) tracks aleatoric/stimulus ambiguity, while jitter variance (perturbed input, same interpretation) tracks epistemic/model uncertainty; in-domain they correlate, out-of-domain they dissociate (jitter rises, spread doesn't), enabling a practical two-dimensional uncertainty readout from one model.
falsifiable_prediction: On in-domain data the two measures will correlate moderately; under increasing shift, jitter variance will rise while multimask spread stays flat or falls; instances high-jitter/low-spread will be enriched for model errors, high-spread/low-jitter for annotator disagreement - a testable 2x2.
why_important: A validated aleatoric/epistemic decomposition from a single frozen model would upgrade routing decisions everywhere (label more vs adapt model vs accept ambiguity) - currently impossible without ensembles.
why_possibly_novel: [HYPOTHESIS] Mapping SAM's two multiplicity mechanisms onto the uncertainty taxonomy and validating the dissociation appears unattempted.
minimal_falsification_experiment: Shift-ladder of datasets + one multi-rater dataset: compute both measures per instance; test the dissociation pattern and the 2x2 enrichment predictions.
main_risk: The two measures share machinery (decoder), so contamination between them may blur the clean decomposition.
community_default_belief: SAM has one useful uncertainty signal at best (the IoU head); output multiplicity is not conceptualized in aleatoric/epistemic terms.
why_that_may_be_wrong: The two mechanisms perturb different variables (interpretation vs evidence) - exactly the operational distinction the taxonomy requires; the mapping is natural but unexamined.
fastest_falsification: Six hours: in-domain vs one far-domain, correlation structure of the two measures.

consolidation.territory: T01 SAM / Foundation Model adaptation / PEFT

one_line: SAM's runner-up masks audit datasets: when the top mask disagrees with ground truth but a runner-up matches it, the dataset likely has a systematic label-convention offset.
problem: Dataset label errors and convention quirks are found by manual inspection; no automatic, convention-aware audit tool exists.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] The signature [top-1 wrong, runner-up right] is diagnostic: at instance level it flags label errors; when its rate is elevated dataset-wide with consistent direction (e.g., GT always matches the larger candidate), it reveals convention offsets (holes, granularity) - separable from random noise by directional consistency.
falsifiable_prediction: Injecting synthetic convention offsets and random label errors into a clean dataset will produce distinguishable signatures (directional vs non-directional runner-up-agreement); on real datasets, flagged conventions will be verifiable by inspection with high precision.
why_important: Free dataset QA at foundation-model quality: catches convention mismatches BEFORE they contaminate adaptation training (many 'domain gaps' may actually be convention gaps - links W15-B001-A-008); gives dataset papers an audit artifact.
why_possibly_novel: [HYPOTHESIS] Using a foundation model's ranked alternatives as a convention-vs-noise discriminating audit appears unproposed.
minimal_falsification_experiment: Clean dataset + injected offsets (dilation, hole-filling, part-merge) and injected random errors; compute signature statistics; verify separability; then run on 5 public datasets and manually verify top flags.
main_risk: SAM's own biases (e.g., shadow-binding W15-B001-A-041) could masquerade as dataset conventions; needs bias-corrected null models.
community_default_belief: Ground truth is ground truth: evaluation and training treat labels as correct, and disagreement is model error by definition.
why_that_may_be_wrong: When a strong prior model consistently 'errs' in the same direction against labels, the parsimonious explanation is a convention difference, not correlated model error - the direction statistics can tell them apart.
fastest_falsification: Six hours: synthetic injection separability test; inseparable signatures falsify.

consolidation.territory: T01 SAM / Foundation Model adaptation / PEFT

one_line: Most published PEFT-method rankings for SAM adaptation don't survive per-method learning-rate tuning - a quantifiable replication crisis in miniature.
problem: [KNOWN FACT] PEFT comparisons commonly share one learning rate across methods despite methods differing in effective update scale; the fraction of published rankings that are LR artifacts is unmeasured.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Re-running representative PEFT comparisons (adapter vs LoRA vs prompt-tuning vs LN-tuning on SAM tasks) with per-method LR optimization will overturn or nullify a large fraction of pairwise rankings; ranking instability will correlate with methods' effective-LR mismatch measured via initial update norms.
falsifiable_prediction: At least a third of pairwise method orderings will flip or fall within seed noise after per-method tuning; a cheap diagnostic (relative first-step update norm) will predict which published comparisons are at risk without rerunning them.
why_important: Method-evaluation hygiene with a constructive tool: the risk diagnostic lets readers triage the literature; the field's actual knowledge about PEFT method superiority may be much smaller than its paper count suggests.
why_possibly_novel: [HYPOTHESIS] A systematic LR-confound audit with a predictive risk diagnostic for vision PEFT appears undone (concerns are voiced informally without quantification).
minimal_falsification_experiment: Select 4 method pairs x 3 SAM adaptation tasks; original shared-LR protocol vs per-method 5-point LR grids x 3 seeds; count ranking survivals; validate the update-norm diagnostic.
main_risk: Choice of 'representative' comparisons invites selection-bias criticism; pre-registration of the comparison set mitigates.
community_default_belief: Reported deltas of 1-3 IoU points between PEFT methods reflect method quality; shared-hyperparameter protocols are considered fair because they are uniform.
why_that_may_be_wrong: Uniform hyperparameters are not fair to methods with different optimization geometry - uniformity IS the bias, systematically favoring methods whose update scale matches the chosen LR.
fastest_falsification: One day: one famous pair, one task, full LR grids; if ranking is LR-invariant, the crisis narrative weakens.

consolidation.territory: T01 SAM / Foundation Model adaptation / PEFT

one_line: mIoU ties hide boundary regressions: adaptation methods indistinguishable on mIoU differ dramatically on boundary metrics, flipping conclusions in a predictable direction (parameter-heavier methods win boundaries).
problem: SAM adaptation results are reported almost exclusively as region-overlap metrics; whether method rankings are metric-stable is untested.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Region metrics saturate first and compress method differences; boundary-F re-evaluation of existing method comparisons will reveal significant divergence, systematically favoring methods that adapt spatial-resolution-relevant components - meaning the field's 'method X ≈ method Y' conclusions are metric artifacts.
falsifiable_prediction: Across re-evaluated comparisons, the variance of method differences under boundary-F will exceed that under mIoU by a large factor; ranking flips will concentrate in high-boundary-complexity datasets; the direction of flips will correlate with where methods place capacity.
why_important: Boundary quality is the actual deliverable in medical/industrial use; if rankings are metric-fragile, deployment choices based on mIoU tables are misinformed - and the fix (report both) is free.
why_possibly_novel: [HYPOTHESIS] A systematic metric-fragility audit of the SAM-adaptation literature appears missing; boundary metrics exist but aren't used for method re-ranking.
minimal_falsification_experiment: Re-evaluate 5 public adapted checkpoints (or reproduce 3 comparisons) under {mIoU, boundary-F, HD95}; quantify ranking stability; stratify by boundary complexity.
main_risk: Public checkpoints may not cover comparable settings; reproduction burden could limit scope.
community_default_belief: mIoU differences summarize method quality; if methods tie on mIoU they are interchangeable and the cheaper one should be used.
why_that_may_be_wrong: Region metrics are mathematically insensitive to boundary-band errors for large objects ([KNOWN FACT] boundary band is a small area fraction); ties on a saturating metric carry little information about the unsaturated dimensions users care about.
fastest_falsification: Four hours: 2 checkpoints tied on mIoU, boundary-F comparison; a tie there too weakens the claim.

consolidation.territory: T01 SAM / Foundation Model adaptation / PEFT

one_line: 'SAM fails on X' papers systematically under-prompt: oracle-prompt re-evaluation shrinks reported zero-shot gaps enough to overturn several failure narratives.
problem: Zero-shot SAM baselines in adaptation papers use a fixed cheap prompt policy (1 center point or 1 box); the fraction of reported gap attributable to prompting rather than model capability is unquantified across the literature.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] A standardized prompt-budget curve (1..k points, box, box+points, best-of-multimask) will show that a large share of published 'SAM fails on domain X' gaps closes at modest prompt budgets - reattributing many failures from representation to interface, and revealing which domain failures are real.
falsifiable_prediction: Across 8 domains with published failure claims, median gap closure at 5-prompt oracle will be substantial; residual-gap domains will cluster into interpretable failure families (resolution-bound, convention-bound) rather than scattering randomly.
why_important: Failure attributions drive research investment; a literature-scale correction would redirect effort from 'fixing SAM's perception' to 'fixing prompt policies and conventions' where appropriate - and establish prompt-budget curves as mandatory baselines.
why_possibly_novel: [HYPOTHESIS] A cross-domain, standardized under-prompting audit of published SAM failure claims appears not to exist (individual papers vary prompts ad hoc).
minimal_falsification_experiment: Reproduce zero-shot baselines on 8 claimed-failure domains; evaluate the standardized prompt ladder; report gap-closure distribution and residual-failure taxonomy.
main_risk: Oracle prompting uses GT, so closure fractions are upper bounds on realizable gains - framing must be careful (attribution, not deployment claim).
community_default_belief: Published zero-shot numbers characterize SAM's capability on a domain; prompt policy is a detail that does not change qualitative conclusions.
why_that_may_be_wrong: For an interface-defined model, capability claims are only meaningful relative to interface usage; degenerate prompting measures the interface floor, not the capability - a category error embedded in dozens of papers' motivation sections.
fastest_falsification: Six hours: 2 claimed-failure domains, prompt ladder; if gaps barely move, the audit thesis fails.

consolidation.territory: T01 SAM / Foundation Model adaptation / PEFT

one_line: GT-derived box prompts leak evaluation information asymmetrically: adapted models trained with tight-box protocols gain inflated advantage over zero-shot baselines under box evaluation.
problem: Standard evaluation prompts (boxes from ground-truth masks) inject object-extent information; whether this injection is method-neutral in adaptation comparisons is unexamined.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Fine-tuned models learn to exploit tight-box statistics (box edge = mask boundary within noise), converting the evaluation prompt into a supervisory leak; zero-shot SAM exploits it less; hence box-prompt evaluations systematically overstate adaptation gains, and the overstatement grows with training-protocol/evaluation-protocol match.
falsifiable_prediction: Adding realistic box noise (5-15% jitter, as human boxes have) will shrink measured adaptation gains substantially; the shrinkage will be larger for models trained with tight boxes than with jittered boxes; point-prompt evaluation will show smaller adaptation gains than box evaluation for the same checkpoints.
why_important: Cross-paper adaptation-gain numbers underpin deployment decisions; a protocol-leak correction changes effect sizes across the literature and prescribes noise-injected evaluation as standard.
why_possibly_novel: [HYPOTHESIS] Prompt-protocol leakage as a confound in adaptation evaluation - and its interaction with training protocol - appears unanalyzed.
minimal_falsification_experiment: 3 domains: checkpoints trained with {tight, jittered} boxes; evaluate under {tight, jittered, point} prompts; decompose gain inflation.
main_risk: Realistic human-box noise models matter; use published interactive-annotation noise statistics or collect a small sample.
community_default_belief: GT-box evaluation is a fair, standard protocol; since all methods see the same prompts, comparisons are unbiased.
why_that_may_be_wrong: Same input does not mean same exploitability: training determines how much a model leans on box-boundary priors, so identical evaluation prompts advantage protocol-matched models - a train/test coupling invisible in the tables.
fastest_falsification: Four hours: one adapted checkpoint, tight vs jittered box evaluation; gain invariance falsifies.

consolidation.territory: T01 SAM / Foundation Model adaptation / PEFT

one_line: The missing null baseline: frozen-SAM-encoder + linear/shallow head matches published PEFT methods on a nontrivial fraction of adaptation benchmarks.
problem: PEFT papers compare against other PEFT and full FT, almost never against the cheapest possible baseline (frozen features + tiny head), leaving the actual value-added of weight adaptation unquantified.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] On a meaningful fraction of standard adaptation benchmarks, a probing-class baseline (frozen encoder, shallow convolutional or linear decode head trained on target data) lands within 1-2 IoU of published PEFT numbers - implying those benchmarks measure feature readout, not adaptation, and are uninformative for comparing adaptation methods.
falsifiable_prediction: Running the null baseline across 10 benchmark datasets will find >=3 where it matches PEFT within noise; those datasets will be identifiable a priori by high linear-probe boundary separability (giving a benchmark-informativeness score).
why_important: Cleans the benchmark landscape: informativeness scoring tells the community which datasets can distinguish adaptation methods at all; embarrassing-baseline results historically recalibrate fields.
why_possibly_novel: [HYPOTHESIS] Systematic null-baseline auditing with an a-priori informativeness score for SAM adaptation benchmarks appears undone.
minimal_falsification_experiment: 10 benchmarks: frozen-encoder shallow-head baseline (fixed recipe, no tuning) vs published/reproduced PEFT numbers; compute probe-separability scores; test the predictive relationship.
main_risk: Fair comparison requires matching training data and augmentation exactly to published setups - reproduction effort is the bottleneck.
community_default_belief: PEFT methods add substantial value over frozen features on adaptation benchmarks - otherwise why the hundreds of papers; the frozen baseline is assumed too weak to report.
why_that_may_be_wrong: An assumption maintained by never testing it; strong frozen features + task-specific readout is exactly what probing literature shows to be surprisingly competitive elsewhere.
fastest_falsification: Six hours: null baseline on 2 popular benchmarks; if it loses by >5 IoU on both, the audit likely fizzles.

consolidation.territory: T01 SAM / Foundation Model adaptation / PEFT

one_line: PEFT gains partially reduce to training-time gains: at matched wall-clock optimization budget, method differences shrink because 'efficient' methods simply take more well-tuned steps.
problem: PEFT comparisons match epochs or final performance but rarely match total optimization compute; faster-per-step methods effectively train longer, confounding method quality with budget.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] A visible share of reported inter-method differences in SAM adaptation disappears under matched-compute protocols (equal GPU-seconds including forward/backward cost differences), and the survivor differences concentrate in methods with genuinely different inductive biases (placement, normalization) rather than reparameterizations.
falsifiable_prediction: Under matched-compute re-runs, the distribution of |method deltas| will contract significantly; the contraction will be largest for method pairs with the largest per-step cost differences - a dose-response signature of the confound.
why_important: Compute-fairness is the minimal condition for method comparisons to mean anything; the dose-response test provides literature-triage without full reruns (flag comparisons with large per-step cost gaps).
why_possibly_novel: [HYPOTHESIS] Matched-compute auditing with the cost-gap dose-response analysis for vision PEFT appears unreported.
minimal_falsification_experiment: 4 method pairs x 2 tasks: original protocol vs matched-GPU-seconds protocol x 3 seeds; measure delta contraction vs per-step cost gap.
main_risk: Wall-clock matching is hardware-dependent; report FLOPs-matched as the primary criterion with wall-clock as secondary.
community_default_belief: Epoch-matched or convergence-matched comparisons are fair; per-step cost differences are an efficiency footnote, not a validity threat.
why_that_may_be_wrong: Optimization progress is a function of steps and step quality, not epochs; cheap steps buy more search, which masquerades as method superiority in every table that doesn't price it.
fastest_falsification: Six hours: the highest-cost-gap pair at matched FLOPs; persistent gap weakens the confound claim.

consolidation.territory: T01 SAM / Foundation Model adaptation / PEFT

one_line: The SAM-adaptation benchmark suite is effectively one benchmark: method rankings across popular datasets are so correlated that multi-dataset tables add almost no evidence.
problem: Papers demonstrate generality via many datasets; if datasets rank methods near-identically, the implied statistical independence is illusory and generality claims are overcounted.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Across published and reproduced results, between-dataset rank correlation of adaptation methods is very high within domain families (e.g., endoscopy sets, CT sets), such that the effective number of independent evaluations in a typical 8-dataset table is 2-3 - computable via ranking-correlation eigenanalysis.
falsifiable_prediction: A meta-analysis matrix (methods x datasets) will show one dominant ranking component within families; a new method's rank on one family member will predict its rank on others with high accuracy - validated prospectively on a held-out dataset.
why_important: Changes how evidence is counted in reviews and how benchmark suites should be constructed (maximize ranking diversity, not dataset count); provides a public effective-evaluations calculator.
why_possibly_novel: [VERIFIED PRIOR WORK] Benchmark-correlation analyses exist for classification leaderboards; [HYPOTHESIS] applying effective-dimension analysis to SAM-adaptation tables and prospectively validating it appears new.
minimal_falsification_experiment: Assemble results matrix from published tables + targeted reproductions; eigenanalysis of rank correlations; prospective prediction test on one newly evaluated dataset.
main_risk: Published tables are sparse/incomparable (different protocols); reproduction subset must anchor the analysis.
community_default_belief: Each additional dataset in a results table is additional independent evidence of method generality.
why_that_may_be_wrong: Datasets within a family share the properties that determine method advantages (modality, label style, difficulty), making their verdicts statistically redundant - a standard meta-analytic point the field's table culture ignores.
fastest_falsification: Four hours with published tables only: if cross-dataset rank correlations are low, the redundancy claim dies immediately.

consolidation.territory: T01 SAM / Foundation Model adaptation / PEFT

one_line: The random-encoder control nobody runs: LoRA-adapting a frozen RANDOM-weight encoder quantifies how much of 'foundation model adaptation' is just any-features-plus-training.
